29.name: OpenStack Academy
29.description: With a focus on education and training for cloud operators and application developers, the OpenStack Academy brings together hands-on workshops and day-long intensive training sessions under one roof. Workshops and trainings require an RSVP and certain pre-requisites. Bring your laptop and walk away with OpenStack skills.

30.name: The Forum
30.description:
At The Forum, OpenStack users and developers in equal parts gather to brainstorm the requirements for the next release, gather feedback on the past version and have strategic discussions that go beyond just one release cycle. Development teams, working groups and interested individuals will discuss release requirements, connect with community members about cross-project collaboration, and to exchange feedback between design and operations members. These are collaborative, interactive group working sessions.

* Note: these are not selected through the Call for Presentations process and submission is limited to WG chair/leader

31.name: Business & Strategy
31.description: IT leaders building their cloud business case are facing unique requirements to move faster and control costs within the bounds of industry regulations and business realities. For business decision makers and those who are interested in topics like financial impact, organizational change, and business products to enhance and support your deployment, case studies in this track are presented from a business perspective, where you can learn why and how organizations adopted OpenStack.

32.name: Architecture & Operations
32.description: For cloud architects, operators and administrators who are looking for technical sessions--ranging from beginner to advanced--that will help you improve your current deployment, learn new tools or understand how to get an OpenStack cloud up and running.

33.name: Developers
33.description: The Developers category will cover developing cloud applications, making the most of containers, delivering valuable services like big data analytics, as well as presentations and help getting started for upstream contributors. Please note that Project Updates will no longer be open to submissions through the Call for Presentations; PTLs will be programming this content for the Boston Summit.

51.name: Open Source Days
51.description: We’ve invited many open source communities to host Open Source Days at the Summit, where community leaders will present the latest on their use cases, software roadmap and progress. You can see who has signed on to participate below, and check back in March for the full agenda.

events.title: OpenStack Upstream Institute, Sponsored by Lenovo (Day 1)
events.body:
OpenStack Upstream Institute is an intensive program designed to share knowledge about the different ways of contributing to OpenStack like providing new features, writing documentation, participating in working groups, and so forth. The educational program is built on the principle of open collaboration and will teach the students how to find information and navigate the intricacies of the project’s technical tools and social interactions in order to get the contributions accepted. The live one and a half day class is focusing on hands-on practice like the students can use a development environment to work on real-life bug fixes or new features and learn how to test, prepare and upload them for review. The attendees are also given the opportunity to join a mentoring program to get further help and guidance on their journey to become an active and successful member of the OpenStack community.

Please note that OpenStack Upstream Institute is a 2 Day program. An RSVP to Day 1 is an automatic RSVP to Day 2. In order to RSVP, you must log in with your OpenStackID and associate your EventBrite order with your OpenStackID.

events.title: RSVP REQUIRED: Canonical Afternoon Training - Telco Cloud Architecture Workshop
events.body:
RSVP REQUIRED: https://canonicalsundayafternoontraining.eventbrite.com

In this workshop we'll look at the right architecture for OpenStack clouds to meet the needs of the world's most demanding Telcos. Drawing on 5 years of experience building clouds for carriers such as Deutsche Telekom, Tele2, Etisalat, Bell Canada and more, lead architects from Canonical will look at the architecture considerations for different types of Telco clouds, getting the balance right between performance, complexity and manageability and how to manage the operations of clouds that have extremely high uptime and redundancy requirements. The workshop will be interactive drawing on on the different viewpoints of how a Telco cloud can be constructed. Attendees are encouraged to bring an opinion.

events.title: Costs Less, Does More
events.body:
It's a multi-cloud world, and OpenStack is becoming an increasingly important part of the mix. From the datacenter to the edge to IoT devices, OpenStack clouds are being deployed to meet more use cases than ever before. Smart organizations are getting more sophisticated about how they place workloads across their cloud portfolio. Learn about how new consumption models, technologies and culture are driving the second generation of private clouds and where it should fit in your cloud portfolio.

Jonathan Bryce will be joined by AT&T, eBay, GE, MIT, Red Hat, US Army Cyber School, Verizon to kick off the OpenStack Summit by demonstrating how the programmable infrastructure platform “Costs Less, Does More.” He’ll also discuss the latest updates on OpenStack, including how the community is organizing to continue to mature, grow and address challenges.

materials.title: Costs Less, Does More

events.title: GE Healthcare Accelerates to Cloud on Openstack Platform
events.body: When your business supports many legacy apps and you want the cost model of cloud but the challenges of force fitting into AWS is not worth the return? Where do you turn? How long do you have to wait for a viable solution? And how much rework?

materials.title: GE Healthcare Accelerates to Cloud on Openstack Platform

events.title: Taking OpenStack Out to the Network Edges
events.body: Think OpenStack only works in data centers and test beds?   Think again.  The Virtual Network Services product leverages OpenStack components as its underlying platform to create a massively distributed Network as a Service solution.

materials.title: Taking OpenStack Out to the Network Edges

events.title: The U.S. Army Cyber School: Saving Millions & Achieving Educational Freedom Through OpenStack
events.body:
The United States Army Cyber School (USACYS) trains and educates Soldiers to defend the interests of the United States and our allies at home and abroad via means grounded in computer science, electrical engineering, robotics, and mathematics. Over the past 18 months, USACYS has used OpenStack to execute this critical mission for force readiness.

This presentation will show our journey from 3 borrowed servers connected to users via CAT6 cables running through a drop ceiling to a 2000-core cluster backed by a 4PB Ceph array that is 100% code-driven. We will also discuss and provide a live demonstration of our CI pipeline that integrates our Blackboard LMS, Heat, and our asciidoc-based curriculum-as-code repository into a student experience that is always up-to-date, relevant, and technically accurate while investing minimum man-hours for content curation. This DevOps-oriented approach, underpinned by OpenStack, allows our instructors to focus on teaching students and creating new content, not creating slide presentations and formatting word processor documents. This approach has yielded high benefits in courseware quality and student outcomes while saving millions of dollars in platform TCO expenses. The OpenStack solution has put USACYS years ahead of similar government education programs and on track to continue to embrace innovation and change for the benefit of national defense.

materials.title: The U.S. Army Cyber School: Saving Millions & Achieving Educational Freedom Through OpenStack

events.title: Nutanix - Cloud Builders Wanted:  OpenStack on Nutanix Enterprise Cloud
events.body:
Need the right infrastructure to realize the value of your OpenStack deployments more quickly and simply? Nutanix leverages a hybrid delivery model to capitalize on public cloud advantages while retaining the security and control of private datacenters. The Nutanix Enterprise Cloud integrates server, storage, virtualization and networking in a turnkey appliance to run any workload at any scale -- removing the complexity of legacy infrastructure.

In this session, see a live demo that proves how easy day-2 datacenter operations are when using Nutanix in an OpenStack powered cloud. The combined approach offers you the best of both worlds: OpenStack's open API for provisioning automation, with the ease of operations provided by the industry leading hyperconverged infrastructure platform. This combination enables you to build a private or public cloud that delivers the agility you want, at the costs you need.

materials.title: Nutanix - Cloud Builders Wanted:  OpenStack on Nutanix Enterprise Cloud

events.title: Around the World in 80 Commits:  Working with a Global Team and Global Community
events.body: Working with remote teams is not always easy:  different timezones, different communication styles, different cultures.  But what do you do when your immediate team is remote and you're working with a worldwide open source community?  The IBM mainframe OpenStack team is spread across three continents (NA, Asia and Europe) and has faced a fair share of challenges with integrating their team together and into the OpenStack community.  Over the past year, AT&T launched a new distributed team of Community contributors. They also initiated a new working group with globally distributed participation. They have been struggling with the challenges of working effectively as a team across a diverse geographies and cultures.  The discussion will deal with tips for tools and teamwork.  We'll also talk about what challenges we still face.  At the end there will be plenty of time for audience questions and a panel style discussion.
events.learning: Attendees should expect to learn what's worked and hasn't worked for two companies managing distributed teams across OpenStack.  They'll discover tools and techniques that have made these companies successful.  They'll also get a chance to ask questions about their own challenges.

materials.title: Around the World in 80 Commits:  Working with a Global Team and Global Community

events.title: Canonical - How PCCW Used cPlane Networks and Ubuntu OpenStack to Deliver Scalable, High-Performance Cloud Infrastructure
events.body: Learn how global Telcos such as PCCW, the leading Telco in Hong Kong, Deutsche Telekom and many others are using OpenStack for carrier grade clouds. In this session you will hear how Canonical and CPLANE NETWORKS have created a hyper-distributed cloud solution for service providers with a differentiated edge-cloud offering for applications connecting with IoT devices. In this session we'll talk through how OpenStack delivers cloud services in the central opffice and at the edge, how telcos are using them in production and what the future holds for OpenStack based Telco clouds

materials.title: Canonical - How PCCW Used cPlane Networks and Ubuntu OpenStack to Deliver Scalable, High-Performance Cloud Infrastructure

events.title: Cloud Dataverse: Data Repository Software for Open Clouds
events.body:
In the last 10 years, the Dataverse project has been a leader in open-source repository software for sharing and archiving research data. Dataverse has an active, growing community of developers and users, with 22 installations of the software around the world. The Harvard Dataverse repository alone hosts 70,000 datasets, 330,000 data files, with contributions from more than 500 institutions.

Cloud Dataverse combines Dataverse and OpenStack by storing datasets in OpenStack’s Swift Object storage and replicating datasets from Dataverse repositories world-wide to the cloud(s) -- offering enormous value to both the Dataverse and OpenStack communities. It provides Dataverse users the ability to host larger datasets and efficiently compute on data from around the world using OpenStack’s compute services. It provides OpenStack users with a repository system that is much richer than Amazon’s Public Datasets service.

materials.title: Cloud Dataverse: Data Repository Software for Open Clouds

events.title: Cloudify Architecture and Roadmap
events.body: Join the Cloudify developers to learn how Cloudify is built from the inside in conjunction with many other open source applications. We will also present a future-looking roadmap detailing where the project is moving and what it plans to accomplish.

events.title: Consuming Multiple OpenStack Clouds with Ease
events.body:
One of the most important value propositions of OpenStack is freedom from vendor lock-in. In order for that to be a tangible benefit and not merely an abstract promise, one needs to be able to interact with multiple clouds at the same time. Luckily, this is not only possible, it's easy.

This session will demonstrate how to treat regions of multiple different OpenStack clouds like they are regions of one big happy cloud. Because I'm insane, all the demos will be live and global.

It'll be 2 shade talks - but I'll make one a talk/discussion of why/design and the other a strict howto/demo.

As far as scheduling goes - I've got holes Monday from 1pm-3:40pm, 12:30pm-3:30pm Wednesday and after 12:30pm on Thursday. Any of those times work? I could also, if necessary, miss the 4:40 and 5:30 slots on Monday, 9-10:30 Wednesday, but I'd prefer not to.

materials.title: Consuming Multiple OpenStack Clouds with Ease

events.title: Deploying Designate for Disaster Recovery
events.body: Disaster recovery (DR) is one of most important use cases that we hear from our customers. Setting up multi region designate for disaster recovery scenario significantly minimizes the impact on dns data in the event of disaster, as designate pushes customer zones across multiple regions so that the customer will be unaffected in case of disaster in one region. In this session we will see how designate can be configured in multi regions for disaster recovery in public cloud environment . And also showcase a small demo on how designate feature and services can be leveraged for disaster recovery process.
events.learning: Setting up multi region designate for disaster recovery scenario significantly minimizes the impact on dns data in the event of disaster This talk helps the audience to understand on various designate features and also how to setup designate in multi region environment

materials.title: Deploying Designate for Disaster Recovery

events.title: Forum 101 (previously "Design Summit 101")
events.body:
First time at the summit? Not a problem! There's lots of people in the same situation.

Come join some of the more experienced members of our community for a gentle hands-on introduction to participating in the Forum.

Welcome, and we hope you have a good time with OpenStack.

events.title: How RDO Uses Software Factory and Ansible
events.body: Abstract: Software-Factory is a collection of services that provides a powerful platform to build software. It enables the same workflow used to develop OpenStack: using Gerrit for code reviews, Zuul/Nodepool/Jenkins as a CI system, and Storyboard for stories and issues tracker.

materials.title: How RDO Uses Software Factory and Ansible

events.title: Hybrid Cloud War Stories: Building a Next-Gen TV and Media Platform Using OpenStack and AWS
events.body:
This session will detail the operational and technical challenges SkyTV (New Zealand's leading TV provider) have had in introducing OpenStack to their environment: from creating a specialised 'Cloud Ops' team to run and manage the platform all the way through to educating the wider business about the operational benefits OpenStack would provide.
Details will be provided on the technical solution put in place, and how SkyTV have used Heat, Ansible & other automation technologies to rapidly provision, update and manage complex application and networking environments across both public and private clouds. SkyTV have built a truly hybrid cloud platform based on OpenStack and AWS, and we want to share their expertise on how to make development and deployment processes seamless across both platforms.
events.learning:
Attendees should expect to learn how to start the 'journey' of bringing an OpenStack cloud into production. This includes some gotchas, how to bring and keep the company along for the ride and maintaining harmony with developers and IT ops.

There will also be the opportunity to learn how OpenStack can seamlessly fit into an existing CI/CD pipeline driven by Bamboo.

Automation experts can learn how to start maximising the usage of Heat with robust templates that produce a complex, multi-tiered architecture across many networks and projects. There will be discussion around how to drive Heat with Ansible and make sure that the right tool is doing the right job. 

Attendees will also have access to versions of the Heat templates and scripts used in the SkyTV environment, shared via GitHub.

materials.title: Hybrid Cloud War Stories: Building a Next-Gen TV and Media Platform Using OpenStack and AWS

events.title: Image Build as a Service: Why It Makes Sense to Build Your Own Cloud Images
events.body:
What if the community or vendor provided cloud images do not fit your requirements?
Like when your cloud needs to offer

  • high performance drivers
  • additional security hardening
  • support for different hypervisors
  • images with latest available patches
  • cloud-specific preconfiguration (e.g. repositories)

For our public cloud "Open Telekom Cloud" we decided to build our own images. Utilizing open-source tools like OpenBuildService, kiwi, DiskImageBuilder, OpenStack tools, adn git we build public images, optimized to run on OTC.
This includes fully automated build, testing and publishing of the images. Following this approach we are able to adapt changes fast, including security patches, hardening and customization.

The image configurations are signed and published along with the resulting images.
This session presents how we build images and how you could build upon this work to set up your own factory, maybe extending it to build container images as well?
events.learning:
The Openstack community and most vendors provide cloud-ready OS images, but modifications are often required to make them fit well to the requirements of the underlying cloud.
In OTC we build our own images because upstream images are lacking important features like e.g. high performance drivers and support for hypervisors besides of KVM.
In this session we present, why it makes sense to build you own cloud images.
And what are the important pieces for an own Image Build Environment setup.

Learnings:

* Requirements for having own cloud images
* Architecture and Setup of an ImageFactory Build Environment
* Ways to automate testing of the images
* Where to get the OTC cloud images and make use of them

materials.title: Image Build as a Service: Why It Makes Sense to Build Your Own Cloud Images

events.title: Kubernetes on OpenStack on Kubernetes: The Infrastructure Club Sandwich
events.body:
OpenStack on Kubernetes? Kubernetes on OpenStack? How about Kubernetes on OpenStack on Kubernetes? This fun and technical session will go over some reference architectures of Kubernetes in conjunction with OpenStack both above and below.  

We review the requirements and challenges of OpenStack which can be solved by using Kubernetes, as well as the needs of providing Kubernetes on top of the IaaS layers to satisfy both infrastructure and developer requirements.
events.learning:
Attendees wil come away with:

  • Understanding of the architectural choices needed to host Kubernetes workloads
  • Knowledge of the Kubernetes underlying infrastructure needed to support the OpenStack control layer
  • Requirements that drive the multi-layer approach

materials.title: Kubernetes on OpenStack on Kubernetes: The Infrastructure Club Sandwich

events.title: Learnings from Scaling OpenStack Ironic at Yahoo
events.body:
Yahoo has hundreds and thousands of servers in data centers. Recently we deployed openstack ironic to manage some of these hardware. As we imported new nodes into ironic, we faced number of challenges related to scale. In this talk we will talk about how we scaled and optimized components such nova-compute, ironic-conductor, neutron-dhcp-agent and solved problems related to baremetal provisioning

 

The talk will have five key components:

1. Problems with nova-compute in scale and how we solved them

2. Scaling neutron-dhcp-agent with dhcpd driver

3. Scaling ironic-conductors 

4. Dealing with hardware/firmware and ipmi issues in the data centers

5. Future work.
events.learning: People who are interested in large scale systems. Openstack Ironic.

materials.title: Learnings from Scaling OpenStack Ironic at Yahoo

events.title: Operating the VM and Baremetal platform (1/2)
events.body:
In this session we bring together the developers of the VM and Baremetal platform (the VM & BM working group) with those who operate the platform, and invite them to join in with the efforts of the working group.

The scope is looking at the constellation of projects that includes: Nova, Neutron, Cinder, Glance, Ironic, Keystone and all the related projects those projects works well together. There is a separate session proposed to cover API user issues, this is focusing on the operator view of the platform.

The session is likely to be structured like this:

* Agree the initial scope of the working group
* Review current efforts, agree a top 5 (or top 10) from the operator point of view
* Get detailed feedback on the top 5
* Recruit user advocates for each effort (folks to help review specs, and generally discuss the implementation with the developers in the weeks/months after the Forum)

Ideally in a second session, the next day, we look at:

* Discuss what is not on the dev radar, but should be
* Determine how the priority of those stack up against the current top 5
* Start initial discussions and recruit advocates for a top 5 of these ideas

After the forum, we follow up this discussion by:

* working together, agreeing specs, refining details, tracking key bugs
* at the PTG, make progress on some of the ideas that are not currently on the dev radar, ideally recruit people to work on them
* come back to the next forum to review the progress, direction and lists of things that are progressing, dig into the next things that need working on

events.title: OPNFV Vision, Community, and Projects
events.body: The Open Platform for Network Functions Virtualization (OPNFV) project within the Linux Foundation is uniquely positioned to bring together the work of open source communities and standards bodies, and commercial suppliers to deliver a de facto NFV platform for the industry. Hear the overall vision for OPNFV, learn how the technical community functions, and get an understanding of the areas covered by 50+ active projects.

events.title: Project Update - Barbican
events.body:
Join the Project Team Leader of Barbican and core contributors for a project update reflecting current developments in the Pike cycle and discussion of future development activity.

We dig into major issues and user needs, and how those needs can be addressed in current and future development. We also discuss hot topics from the Project Teams Gathering, and major development decisions agreed by the team.

Get an in-depth look at the top features and enhancements Barbican plans to deliver in the Pike release in August. Then look beyond Pike to the Queens and “R” releases to learn more about major development themes such as scalability, manageability, resiliency and user experience that the team intends to tackle in the long term.

 

Developers who are interested in contributing to this project are strongly encouraged to attend, as are users and product managers who want to know more about this project’s latest features, their value to users, and the development team’s roadmap.

Questions and discussion are encouraged from the audience, and this presentation will become part of OpenStack’s project navigator at openstack.org/software/project-navigator.

materials.title: Project Update - Barbican

events.title: Red Hat - Deterministic Storage Performance: 'The AWS Way' for Capacity-Based QoS with OpenStack and Ceph
events.body: Managing storage quality of service is a hot topic among operators of OpenStack systems. Tenants demand that their private cloud environments provide familiar public cloud modalities, including the ability to provision deterministic storage performance. This talk will detail how Ceph storage pools can be combined with Cinder Volume Types to emulate Amazon’s Magnetic and Provisioned IOPS Elastic Block Store (EBS). Performance graphs will detail when size based limits, or fixed limits are more appropriate, depending on the type of storage media used in the underlying Ceph pool.

materials.title: Red Hat - Deterministic Storage Performance: 'The AWS Way' for Capacity-Based QoS with OpenStack and Ceph

events.title: Scalable LBaaS Backend: Using Kubernetes and ECMP
events.body:
The number of compute nodes handled in our OpenStack region are increasing from hundreds to thousands.
In such condition, load balancers are required to scale out flexibly as traffic increases.
However, it is difficult to realize these functions using traditional master-slave hardware loadbalancer
So, we developed and deployed scalable software load balancer in our production environment.

This load balancer system can increase capacity by just adding LB-node.
We developed the following components to realize the function:
- IP Fabric: The network that have capabilities of High bandwidth and ECMP(Equal Cost Multipath)
- ECMP: Incoming packets are distributed to each LB-node
- Bird: Advertising VIP to IP Fabric with BGP
- LB-node: Commodity server
- Kuberntes: Orchestration suitable for distributed environment

We will present the architecture and findings gained from this initiative.
events.learning:
- Thinking and designing about the development of load balancer to scale out.
- Architecture and findings gained by using load balancer with Kubernetes.

materials.title: Scalable LBaaS Backend: Using Kubernetes and ECMP

events.title: The Truth About Interop: Running Cloud Foundry on OpenStack
events.body:
According to the 2016 OpenStack survey, Cloud Foundry is the second most popular workload on OpenStack for managing applications. To ensure that Cloud Foundry runs on different OpenStack distributions and configurations is an important and classic interop example.

From the OpenStack side, we see efforts towards interoperability between different OpenStack installations: There are challenges done by the foundation, as live on stage at the Barcelona summit. There is RefStack, defining a set of requirements to meet before a product can use the 'OpenStack' brand. These efforts, however, are currently not enough. The challenges focus on small example applications and use a compatibility library to hide the differences. The RefStack tests don't cover all necessary functionality.

For most people, the truth about the state of interop is a hard one: They go through a long list of manual steps to configure their OpenStack installation and then try to install and run Cloud Foundry on it. When it fails, you have to be a Cloud Foundry expert to figure out what needs to be changed in OpenStack.

We developed the CF OpenStack Validator as an executable with a single configuration file, which runs a set of tests to make sure you can deploy and run open-source Cloud Foundry on your OpenStack installation. If a test doesn't pass, the validator gives actionable feedback on what to change in your OpenStack configuration. If you're installing a commercial product which extends open-source Cloud Foundry, you can extend the validator with additional tests, such as the usage of Swift as blobstore.

Our team is also maintaining the OpenStack abstraction layer for BOSH, the tool which is used to install Cloud Foundry and the promise is to support the three most recent versions of OpenStack. Therefore, the CF OpenStack validator has become an incredibly useful tool for us. Whether you are responsible to install Cloud Foundry on an OpenStack installation or maintaining an OpenStack installation where Cloud Foundry is planned as a workload or building a product based on open-source Cloud Foundry: The CF OpenStack validator can also help you.

materials.title: The Truth About Interop: Running Cloud Foundry on OpenStack

events.body: The project onboarding rooms will be set up classroom style, dedicated to the projects that have signed up to teach new contributors about the project code, and give them an opportunity to meet established community members. The idea is that new contributors will come here to get started in the project after they have gone to OpenStack Upstream Institute and already know the basics of contribution.

events.title: Securing Web Applications with Service Chaining
events.body:
Securing a multi-tier web application requires a number of security functions resulting in complex layer 3 networking rules introducing error and network latency. Instead, OpenStack can service chain traffic through security functions using layer 2 constructs to reduce complexity and improve performance.


In this lab, students will be provided with an OpenStack cloud, a vulnerable web application and security functions to protect it (virtualized security machines) to protect a web application. The lab has students configure service chaining to flow traffic through all the required security functions reducing the complexity, latency and operational costs. A vulnerability scanner is available for students to validate that the security functions are indeed in place and protecting the application. This lab is run completely on open source software.

 

Please note:  this session attendance will be limited to 64 people.  All admittance will be on a first come, first served basis.  This session will be repeated on Wednesday, April 10th, at 9am in Back Bay Ballroom C/D.  Thank you for your understanding.
events.learning:
This lab educates attendees on the how to utilize virtual networking to easily introduce network security functions into the traffic flow without having to re-engineer the layer 3 networks. This includes using Heat, Nova and Neutron through the Horizon and OpenStack command line clients

Attendees will also learn how to protect web applications utilizing open source network security software available in the lab as virtual machines. This includes using network vulnerability scanners to validate that the security functions are indeed protecting the website.

events.title: Session Cancelled - Configure Your Cloud for Auto-Recovery
events.body:
All technology fails.  There is no getting around this point.  The part that we can influence out of that statement is what happens when the technology fails.  OpenStack in all its marvelous modular glory can be a bear when you encounter the service failure creep.  You know that think which occurs when one service fails and then causes another service to fail...then on and on.

Imagine if you could configure your OpenStack services to automatically recovery.  Yes, I know you are going to say I can do that with a cron job or something alike.  For a second think of the impact if you could link your monitoring system to another one that will trigger automated recovery processes to restore your OpenStack services without human intervention.

This workshop will walk attendees thru the process of linking a monitoring system such as Nagios to an automated recovery system such as StackStorm to produce auto-recovery OpenStack cloud actions.

 

Please note:  session attendance does have a maximum capacity.  All admittance will be on a first come, first served basis.  Thank you for your understanding.
events.learning:
• Attendees will learn a bit about what services should be monitored with Nagios
  • Learn some baseline threshold you can set for your monitoring events
  • Become familar with StackStorm, an open source triggered auto-remediation tool
  • Explore how you can link the two tools together to setup auto-recovery for your OpenStack services

events.title: Discover All-Flash Ceph for High Performance Storage Pool
events.body:
NUMA topology in storage for OpenStack provide high-level control which help users minimize latency and maximize performance. According to our experience, users are keen to know how to make Ceph run faster for I/O intensive workloads. Many companies are looking for Ceph that can provide high IOPS to run databases or mission critical applications. In order to achieve certain IOPS per Ceph cluster, the conﬁguration of Ceph parameters, PCIe SSDs and hardware plays a critical role. It also drives the demand of the server with NUMA design, which beneﬁts the Ceph performance and lowers the latency.

In this session, we'll share performance analysis and ﬁndings of all-ﬂash Ceph on a NUMA-balanced server when running MySQL workloads. You will learn how a server design and conﬁgurations affect the Ceph performance and best practices to conﬁgure IOPS-optimized Ceph for OpenStack.
events.learning:
• Performance analysis and ﬁndings of all-ﬂash Ceph when running IOPS-intensive workloads on a NUMA-balanced server.
  • Hardware design and conﬁgurations affect the Ceph performance
  • Best practices to conﬁgure IOPS-optimized Ceph.

materials.title: Discover All-Flash Ceph for High Performance Storage Pool

events.title: Turbo Charged VNFs at 40 gbit/s. Approaches to Deliver Fast, Low Latency Networking Using OpenStack
events.body:
High-speed networking, beyond 10 gig in OpenStack is still a very challenging area. OpenStack has 3 possible approaches:  SR-IOV, DPDK enabled virtual switch, or offload via intelligent network adapters. SR-IOV while offering high throughput and low latency, limits advanced features such as VXLAN and MPLS based segmentation, security groups and live migration. DPDK based approaches support live migration, VXLAN and MPLS based segmentation and security groups but require significant host resources in order to
process the packets. Intelligent network adapters offer best of both worlds, fast throughput and advanced features while using minimal host resources.


This presentation will detail advantages and disadvantages of various approaches. We will describe our experience in working with Netronome to integrate Agilio SmartNic with OpenContrail and Mirantis OpenStack, provide comparative benchmarks between vRouter DPDK and Agilio and show a quick demo.
events.learning: Attendees will learn how to build OpenStack networks to deliver 40-gigabit performance, advantages and disadvantages of various high-speed approaches and how to integrate Agilio into OpenStack and Open Contrail and

materials.title: Turbo Charged VNFs at 40 gbit/s. Approaches to Deliver Fast, Low Latency Networking Using OpenStack

events.title: A Series of Unfortunate Deployments: Running a Lambda Architecture on OpenStack
events.body:
We share the harrowing tale of a team of operators, devops engineers, and developers as they pursue their goal of deploying a scalable, high-performance chemistry search engine based on the Lambda architecture in Openstack.  This is not a story for the faint of heart, dear listener.

Tragedies in this talk include:

  •  Laggard networks! (VXLAN/VLAN trade-offs) 
  •  Murderous kernels! (CPU pinning and pre-allocated hugepages) 
  •  Recalcitrant storage! (Cinder backed with flash; Problems found in os-brick and multipathd)
events.learning: This is the story of our team’s efforts to deploy a Lambda architecture search engine on Openstack, showcasing the trials and tribulations we encountered on our journey.  We share both what worked for us and what didn’t.  How taking advantage of all that Nova Compute offers made this deployment a success. We also highlight the importance of the Openstack operators working closely with developers to ensure maximize performance and stability.  Openstack is excellent for all things, but best when both devs and operators tailor the environment to match the expected workloads.

materials.title: A Series of Unfortunate Deployments: Running a Lambda Architecture on OpenStack

events.title: Adobe Advertising Cloud: The Reality of Cloud Bursting with OpenStack
events.body:
After successfully moving a large workload from a Public Cloud to an OpenStack Private Cloud, the former TubeMogul Operations Engineering team tackled its next important step toward Cloud Bursting.

While experiencing hyper-growth on the Adobe Advertising Cloud, the team had to figure out a simple way to quickly provision new compute resources. Our latency critical workload need our core private resources while some workload can safely leverage public cloud. Cloud Bursting helped to ensure rapid support of the business and provide a more flexible capacity planning strategy. Being able to burst some workload back to the Public Cloud allowed the team to leverage the best of public and private cloud.

In this presentation, we will detail how the team dealt with the network complexity between clouds infrastructure, the cost effectiveness of cloud bursting, the impact on performance, and the hard reality of multi-cloud environments.
events.learning:
This talk will cover the technical detail of:

  • Bursting workload from an OpenStack private cloud to AWS public cloud
  • The network constraints and challenges while doing cloud bursting
  • What would be the next steps toward full cloud bursting capabilities with multiple public cloud provider like AWS, Azure, and GCP.
  • Lesson Learned and Post Cost Analysis

materials.title: Adobe Advertising Cloud: The Reality of Cloud Bursting with OpenStack

events.title: Apache ARIA - Open Source, Open Governance Multi-Cloud TOSCA Orchestration
events.body:
Apache ARIA is an, open source, lightweight framework, which includes a library and CLI for implementing orchestration software using the TOSCA specification. ARIA is the core orchestration engine for the Cloudify orchestrator and is also used in the OPEN-O project.

 

The ARIA community was formed to advance adoption of the TOSCA standard and accelerate the industry’s journey towards application orchestration in cloud environments. It was created for application vendors to test TOSCA models on an easy to use, free, and open source orchestrator. It is also intended for enterprises and telecoms interested in TOSCA orchestration to advance the spec adoption and easily demonstrate portable TOSCA orchestration.

events.title: Bifrost: Using Ansible and Ironic to Deploy BareMetal CI
events.body: Did you know you can deploy baremetal with OpenStack using Ansible? Did you know that projects do this to help manage their CI systems for large platform testing?  During this session we will talk about Bifrost, what it can do for you, and how some of these minimalist bare metal clouds have been built for CI purposes.

materials.title: Bifrost: Using Ansible and Ironic to Deploy BareMetal CI

events.title: Canonical - Using Kubernetes and OpenStack for CPU and GPU Intensive Workloads
events.body: It is commonly thought that OpenStack and/or Kubernetes are not appropriate enviropnments for CPU intensive workloads of the types of application that make use of GPUs. In this session Marco will show how applications such as tensorflow or video rendering, managed by Kubernetes running in OpenStack not only delivers performance but can actually improve the overall compute throughput.

materials.title: Canonical - Using Kubernetes and OpenStack for CPU and GPU Intensive Workloads

events.title: Did You Check the Network? Troubleshooting BOSH and Cloud Foundry on OpenStack
events.body:
The goal of any PaaS is to abstract away the underlying hardware or software infrastructure. "Here is my application, I don't care how you deploy it, just get it done!" But your target infrastructure will have its own nuances. This is certainly true for OpenStack.

Having deployed and automated BOSH and Cloud Foundry hundreds of times, over several versions of OpenStack, we at Stark & Wayne have had the opportunity to see many of the edge cases, and constant sources of implementation pain that occur.

We'd are going to share some of our most useful experiences with you.

materials.title: Did You Check the Network? Troubleshooting BOSH and Cloud Foundry on OpenStack

events.title: Kubernetes and OpenStack at Scale
events.body:
Imagine being able to stand up thousands of tenants with thousands of apps, running thousands of Docker-formatted container images and routes, all on a self-healing cluster and elastic infrastructure. Now, take that one step further - all of those images being updatable through a single upload to the registry, and with zero downtime. In this session, you will see just that.

In this presentation, we will walk through a recent benchmarking deployment using Kubernetes and OpenStack on the Cloud Native Computing Foundation’s (CNCF's) 1,000 node cluster with OpenStack and Red Hat’s OpenShift Container Platform, the enterprise-ready Kubernetes for developers. 

You'll also what's been happening in subsequent rounds of testing in Red Hat's own SCALE lab and the CNCF cluster and how we are working with the relevant open source communities including OpenStack, Kubernetes, and Ansible to continue to raise the bar for horizontal scaling of these platforms via community powered innovation.
events.learning:
Attendees will learn about the preparation that was required to run Kubernetes on OpenStack at scale, the architecture of the resultant deployment and some of the issues and best practices identified along the way.

They will also learn how to gain access to the CNCF and OSIC clusters for their own community projects and how the results of these scale testing exercises are being shared with the relevant open source communities as we work together to raise the bar for horizontal scaling of these platforms.

materials.title: Kubernetes and OpenStack at Scale

events.title: Lessons in IPv6 Deployment in OpenStack Environments
events.body:
More operators are deploying OpenStack environments using IPv6 due to the IPv4 address exhaustion. Recent releases of OpenStack supports production quality of IPv6 deployments for tenantsby leveraging the combination of Neutron features.

This session will cover the following topics:

  • IPv6 deployments options and consideration points
  • IPv6 address configuration options and comparisons (SLAAC, DHCPv6 stateless, DHCPv6 stateful)
  • IPv6 global address management: Using neutron subnet pool feature / Using prefix delegation
  • Routing considerations: dynamic routing from upstream router to tenant routers / prevent unauthorized global address
  • Points on IPv4/IPv6 dual stack : Configurations of Additional information like DNS servers, MTU or static routes
  • Both of Neutron reference implementation and third party virtual appliances are discussed.

This session will focus on being a guide on setup and operation on IPv6 deployment.
events.learning:
This session will focus on being a guide on setup and operation on IPv6 deployment. Attendees of this session can get practical guide on IPv6 deployments like below. Examples on detail configuration and command lines will be provided.

  • IPv6 deployments options and consideration points
  • IPv6 address configuration options and comparisons (SLAAC, DHCPv6 stateless, DHCPv6 stateful)
  • IPv6 global address management (neutron subnet pool feature, prefix delegation)
  • Routing considerations
  • Points on IPv4/IPv6 dual stack
  • IPv6 on Neutron refence implementation and third party virtual appliances.

materials.title: Lessons in IPv6 Deployment in OpenStack Environments

events.title: Looking Beyond the Technology: Privacy, Trust and Security in the Cloud
events.body:
The adoption of cloud computing and the migration of applications to the platform is rapidly transforming how businesses and individuals perform their regular day to day functions. More than a trillion dollars will be spent in the next five years, directly or indirectly, to shifting processes to the cloud. According to Gartner, "This will make cloud computing one of the most disruptive forces of IT spending since the early days of the digital age."

As the world rapidly transistions to the cloud, it's important to consider not just the technical advantages this change provides but also think about the potential non-technical risks. This talk looks at the social and political issues surrounding the current state of privacy and security in cloud computing and the trust we place in others.
events.learning:
This talk will attempt to show the current landscape of the cloud, raise existing social and political issues and discuss how corporations and citizens are addressing these concerns. It will also consider the role of privacy and how the cloud can positively and negatively affect security.

The shift to the cloud is upon us and we're at the forefront in development to shaping what it will become.

Disclaimer: There may be a bias in discussion towards North American and Canadian issues considering the country of origin of the presenter.

materials.title: Looking Beyond the Technology: Privacy, Trust and Security in the Cloud

Let us show you the value of TripleO Magic! In place upgrades is only one item in our bag of tricks (that can be YOUR bag of tricks too!) Come join us while we show you how to conjure a rock solid OpenStack environment that has continuous validations running to ensure stability throughout the entire lifecycle of that cloud even THROUGH your in-place upgrade! This isn't a cookie cutter deployment either! Customizations abound! The reference architecture not working for you? Use your magic wand to create custom composable roles and deploy YOUR cloud YOUR way!

events.title: Object Migration from Different Storage Cloud to OpenStack Swift
events.body: One of the key aspects to consider while moving from an on-prem storage system or from a storage cloud to OpenStack swift is how to migrate the existing data to OpenStack swift. This session talks about a tool which one can use to migrate data from an object store and even Filesystem, to OpenStack Swift. This will help user to move to OpenStack Swift easily. The tool is based on OpenStack “On Demand Migration” Middleware (https://review.openstack.org/#/c/64430/) with added support for features like multi-part upload for migrating large objects, S3 ACL and few more. We will also demonstrate migration of data to Openstack Swift as part of this session.
events.learning:
In this talk attendees will learn :
1. About middleware used to fetch objects from source cloud storage.
2. How we automated the entire data migration process using certain drivers.
3. How large objects are migrated from source to openstack swift by doing multi-part upload.
4. How S3 ACL are migrated to openstack swift, and how using swift3 middleware we can access S3 ACL
5. Changes done to libcloud to access S3 acl and addition of new regions.
6. We will also demonstrate some use cases of object migration from S3 to swift, swift to swift and filesystem to swift.

materials.title: Object Migration from Different Storage Cloud to OpenStack Swift

events.title: OpenStack and Windows:  What's new in Ocata
events.body:
OpenStack is a great platform for Linux as well as for Windows, with the latter growing stronger every year as OpenStack gains more momentum in the enterprise world.

Microsoft's Windows Server / Hyper-V Server 2016 includes a lot of new cloud oriented features which are fully supported in an OpenStack infrastructure, including Storage Spaces Direct for hyper-converged deployments, Shielded VMs for the best guest isolation, Nano Server, a new networking stack and much more.

Windows as a guest on any hypervisor, including KVM, Hyper-V, ESXi, is also a great match for OpenStack thanks to Cloudbase-Init's large set of cloud provisioning actions and support for Heat templates, with lots of new features developed during the Ocata timeframe. 

During this session we will talk about all the new OpenStack Windows and Hyper-V related features, demo some great use cases and provide answers to the most common questions about how to make the best out of Windows in OpenStack.
events.learning:
Attendees will learn about new Windows and Hyper-V features in Keystone, Nova, Cinder, Neutron and other OpenStack projects.

The session will also provide a list of answers to common Windows OpenStack questions, especially oriented at people with an OpenStack and Linux background that look at expanding their knowledge into how Windows enterprise requirements can fit in the picture.

materials.title: OpenStack and Windows:  What's new in Ocata

events.title: OpenStack documentation: The future depends on all of us
events.body:
There are ongoing activities to move the current documentation content and responsibilities back to the project teams. Currently, the documentation team helps enable the project teams to write documentation for installation and deployment methods.

The documentation team leads are looking for more dedicated involvement from the cross-project documentation liaisons and the project teams by identifying all the guides that would need to live in project repositories. In addition, the documentation team needs to find new team members and more involvement from the working groups and the user community. The working groups and user community have been particularly identified as they not just the users and testers of the code, but of the documentation material as well.

During the session, we will highlight the current situation and plans for the Pike release. As a next step, we will look into further actions to address the current issues and ensure the quality of our documentation onwards to help deploy, troubleshoot, and operate OpenStack.

We are expecting documentation liaisons, PTL’s, and representatives from our working groups and user community to see how we can leverage the expertise the community has and make the future of the OpenStack documentation/OpenStack Manuals a community effort.

Then, attendees will learn how OPNFV conducts its release planning and execution and get an overview of the milestones, timeline, and process for each major release.

events.title: Fifty Shades of Enrollment:  How to use Certmonger to win OpenStack
events.body:
When securing the Openstack services by deploying them behind TLS, we need to figure out how to automatically obtain and manage the required certificates.  Certmonger has long been used for precisely this purpose, but the instance needs credentials.


This talk will explore how a new Nova micro-service (novajoin) is used to enroll nova instances as FreeIPA clients, which in turn provides the credentials to get certificates for hosts and services. Moreover, we get the abilities to implement centralized host and sudo access controls.
events.learning: Attendees will learn how to use novajoin - a new Nova micro-service, to register Nova instances as IPA clients.  This, in turn, will allow you to use certmonger to issue and manage host and service certficates for TLS, and to enforce centralized host and sudo access control.

materials.title: Fifty Shades of Enrollment:  How to use Certmonger to win OpenStack

events.title: Elastic OpenStack Deployments
events.body:
Applications hosted on OpenStack can scale on demand, but OpenStack deployments are generally static; scaling a deployment up or down typically requires tedious manual intervention. Automated OpenStack provisioning solutions like MaaS, Packstack, FUEL, etc. are geared towards one-time installations where the associated hardware is used only for OpenStack services throughout its lifetime. As a result, the barrier to a company that wants to use OpenStack internally is high, involving a potentially large capital commitment.

We present the Hardware Isolation Layer package (HIL) and Bare Metal Imaging (BMI) solution. (HIL+BMI) allows administrators to rapidly grow/shrink their OpenStackdeployments and lets them reuse any existing hardware with the flexibility to repurpose it for tradition legacy applications. We will share our experience and lessons of hosting multiple OpenStack deployments using (HIL+BMI) in the Massachusetts Open Cloud (MOC). We will discuss how these software frameworks enable reuse of finite hardware resources in our data-center to host OpenStack instances of varied size and (re)purposes, from student projects to research collaboration to long-running production clusters, alongside non-cloud deployments. We will also present use cases demonstrating how HIL and BMI together can be used to improve resource utilization in multi-tenant Data Centers.

materials.title: Elastic OpenStack Deployments
