events.title: EasyStack - ESCaaS 4.0,  Unified Managment Platform of OpenStack and Kubernetes
events.body: Easystack demonstrated multi-tenancy container orchestration capability on bare metal in elastic dedicated cloud in Barcelona Summit. In ESCaaS 4.0, we bring the unified management capability of OpenStack and Kubernetes, user can use k8s beyond and besides OpenStack. From view of k8s, OpenStack provides compute resources including vm and baremetal, unified network resources connecting openstack and kubernetes, storage resources for stateful applications. Based on these, it gives users an opportunity to orchestration applications consist of vm and containers micro services in unified view. ESCaaS 4.0 brings users with various kinds of applications into an unified cloud platform to maximise the heterogeneous resources and infrastructure power.

materials.title: EasyStack - ESCaaS 4.0,  Unified Managment Platform of OpenStack and Kubernetes

events.title: User Fundamentals I & II: The OpenStack Dashboard and OpenStack Client
events.body: New to OpenStack? This session will give a quick overview of how to use the two most popular ways to interact with OpenStack: The Horizon Dashboard and the OpenStack Client. Learn how to authenticate with an OpenStack installation, and manage your compute, network, and storage resources with these intuitive interfaces.

materials.title: User Fundamentals I & II: The OpenStack Dashboard and OpenStack Client

events.title: StackStorm - If-This-Then-That for DevOps Automation
events.body:
StackStorm - If-This-Then-That for DevOps automation

You may have heard that event driven automation helps Facebook save 16,000 person-hours in operations each day. Do you ever wonder “How can I accomplish this in my OpenStack cluster? How can I optimize operations and integrate multiple DevOps toolchains?" The answer is StackStorm - an open-source, Apache 2.0 licensed, event driven automation platform. Sometimes called “IFTTT for DevOps”, StackStorm is built on the same principles as Facebook’s FBAR. StackStorm provides DevOps teams a powerful, flexible, and reliable platform that enables moving beyond simple “scripts” into automation that is driven by input from other software systems. In addition to optimizing operations, Enterprise users leverage StackStorm to automate their growing infrastructure, private and public cloud deployments, network infrastructure, and security.

In this presentation, you will get an overview of StackStorm, see event driven automation in action, touch on ChatOps, and even get to talking about Serverless use cases for StackStorm.


About the speaker:

Dmitri Zimine, CTO and co-founder of StackStorm, currently is responsible for automation at Brocade (Brocade acquired StackStorm in 2016). Under his leadership, the StackStorm engineering team continues to grow StackStorm open-source, and is re-defining the network automation space with Brocade Workflow Composer.
At OpenStack, Dmitri is one of the creators and original contributors to Mistral, the OpenStack Workflow Service.

materials.title: StackStorm - If-This-Then-That for DevOps Automation

events.title: Cloudify - Hybrid Orchestration: Automation Across and Between Heterogenous Platforms
events.body: There has been an explosion of application platforms in recent years, from containers, to virtualization, to cloud platforms. Often, each platform has its own orchestration tools to deal with automation requirements to serve the needs of DevOps teams. Real world environments usually consist of combinations of such platforms. This talk and demo will present orchestration that spans multiple platforms, in this case Kubernetes on bare metal and Openstack virtual machines.

materials.title: Cloudify - Hybrid Orchestration: Automation Across and Between Heterogenous Platforms

events.title: Introducing ONAP
events.body:
ONAP (Open Network Automation Platform) in a new open source networking initiative under the Linux Foundation, fusing their two flagship open source networking projects Open-O, and open source ECOMP, and is quickly becoming the fastest growing networking project backed by many carriers and network providers. ONAP will allow end users to automate, design, orchestrate, and manage services and virtual functions.

 

In this session, you will have a chance to hear about the project architecture and key components, including a live demo. We will end the session with an open discussion with representatives from ONAP’s Platinum member companies.

events.title: Ansible: Community, Collaboration, and the OpenStack Modules You Know and Love
events.body:
Ansible is an open source project that makes automation simple -- and it just happens to be the #1 tool reported by users for deployment and configuration of OpenStack. Want to learn about how the OpenStack and Ansible communities collaborate to make this possible? Want to hear about the other ways Ansible’s 2600+ contributors have simplified automation for just about anything you can imagine? This session is for you. And if you’re thinking of using Ansible to *consume* an OpenStack cloud, or if you’ve heard about the legendary OpenStack Modules for Ansible and want to know more -- this session is for you, too!  And for anyone who wants to know the basics of what this “Ansible thing” they keep hearing of is all about.

 

Come to this session, and you can:

 

  • Find out what’s new in the Ansible project and community (hint: Containers! Kubernetes! Networking!)

  • Get a whirlwind tour of All Things Ansible-powered in the OpenStack community.

  • Learn how Ansible’s OpenStack modules, powered by the legendary Shade library, make consuming your cloud *easy*. Don’t know what a module is? Don’t worry, we’ll cover that too.

  • Discover how the Ansible and OpenStack communities work together in the development of Ansible’s OpenStack modules, and how you can help.

  • Ask that One Burning Question that Robyn knows you’re going to ask…

 

Also: there may be squirrels. (But don’t worry, they are awesome squirrels.)

materials.title: Ansible: Community, Collaboration, and the OpenStack Modules You Know and Love

events.title: Building and Using Private Clouds in Retail
events.body: Many retail companies struggle to remain relevant in a changing market. Embracing Openstack can enable companies to move faster in all facets of their business. From online sales, to web point of sale in stores, and even pipeline and manufacturing capabilities.
events.learning: How Gap, Inc. uses private cloud and the benefits its business units see from its use. How Gap, Inc. has enabled devops, user self service, and a multi-billion dollar omini pipeline using Openstack.

materials.title: Building and Using Private Clouds in Retail

events.title: Canonical - Hybrid Cloud Kubernetes
events.body: Join this session to learn how you can use Kubernetes for application deployment and management across OpenStack, VMware and public clouds. Containers and cloud go hand in hand and your container infrastructure strategy will need cover both on premises and public clouds. In this session, Canonical's Kubernetes product lead Mark Shuttleworth will show how you can deliver container container orchestration systems across both public and private clouds with ease with scalable operations and costs.

materials.title: Canonical - Hybrid Cloud Kubernetes

events.title: Evolving the Community-Generated Roadmap
events.body: The Product Work Group has assembled a roadmap almost exclusively formed by developers, as PTLs submitted their key features/enhancements for the next release, and predicted major areas of development for future releases. But this neglected the full loop of feedback between users and devs, and it didn't direct development priorities (just reflected current state). How can the Forum fuel a better roadmap to inform our wider community and reflect key user needs?

events.title: How OPNFV Uses OpenStack & How it’s Useful
events.body: OpenStack has been a part of OPNFV from the start and the OpenStack and OPNFV communities have strong areas of overlap. We will explain OPNFV from an Openstack and practical perspective, providing a specific example (SFC scenario) of how we are daily testing different components of OpenStack and other communities (ODL, OVS, etc). We’ll also talk about how OPNFV is useful to OpenStack because (hint: telco requirements & testing) and briefly describe several OPNFV projects which have contributed to OpenStack: NetReady, Multisite, Doctor, Cross CI, Copper, etc.

events.title: Ironic Feedback (Bare Metal & Networking)
events.body: Get operators, deployers, users, and developers together to talk about Ironic. What's good? What's terrible? What do folks need to make their life better? Also possibly discuss how we can improve the feedback loop between these groups of people - ideally we would be talking more than 2-4 times a year.

events.title: On the Fly Service Deployment by a Service Broker Using Heat Orchestration Templates
events.body:
Applications that are deployed to the Cloud Foundry platform often rely on external services like databases to provide their functionality. The performance and reliability of these services are therefore key elements in the user experience of the app. Cluster deployments of these services within OpenStack are the preferred way to accomplish these goals. However the manual deployment and removal of these services can be cumbersome and error prone. To circumvent these flaws the service broker itself should be responsible for the correct just in time deployment of these services on OpenStack. To this end services are deployed when service instances are created in Cloud Foundry using Heat Orchestration Templates.

In this talk Christian Brinker and Sebastian Böing present how services like MongoDB Replica Sets or RabbitMQ Clusters can be dynamically deployed inside OpenStack and availability to Cloud Foundry can be achieved using an existing open source service broker framework.

materials.title: On the Fly Service Deployment by a Service Broker Using Heat Orchestration Templates

events.title: OpenStack and OVN: What's New with OVS 2.7
events.body:
OVN is a virtual networking project built by the Open vSwitch community.
OpenStack can make use of OVN as its backend networking implementation
for Neutron. OVN and its Neutron integration are ready for use in OpenStack
deployments.

This talk will cover the latest developments in the OVN project and the
latest release, part of OVS 2.7. Enhancements include better performance,
improved debugging capabilities, and more flexible L3 gateways.
We will take a look ahead the next set of things we expect to work on for
OVN, which includes logging for OVN ACLs (security groups), encrypted
tunnels, native DNS integration, and more.

We will also cover some of the performance comparison results of OVN
as compared with the original OVS support in Neutron (ML2/OVS). Finally,
we will discuss how to deploy OpenStack with OVN or migrate an existing
deployment from ML2/OVS to OVN.
events.learning: Attendees will learn the latest developments about OVN and how they may be used for OpenStack Networking deployments.

materials.title: OpenStack and OVN: What's New with OVS 2.7

events.title: OpenStack is Also Open to Chip Architecture: See How ARM64 Based Chips Can Add Value
events.body:
OpenStack is the lead Open Source solution for Private Clouds and this has been recognised by many hardware providers who have made there technologies work with the code.

Most are aware of the heavy use of ARM based technology in the IoT side of Cloud architectures but what many may not realise is that ARM64 based server technology offers capabilities that may well make strong technical and economic sense to Architects looking to build solutions based on OpenStack.

Walk through the use cases where the ARM64 chip offer Cloud based applications specific capabilities that could make the difference between success and failures in your clouds.
events.learning: There is often a presumption that ARM chip technologies are only relavent to Cloud Architects for Network or IoT considerations. See how ARM is now using the ARM64 based chips with it's partners to deliver fully supported enterprise ready OpenStack, Compute, Network and Storage options.

materials.title: OpenStack is Also Open to Chip Architecture: See How ARM64 Based Chips Can Add Value

events.title: Project Update - Cinder
events.body:
Join the Project Team Leader of Cinder and core contributors for a “project update” reflecting on the Ocata cycle and additional discussion of future development activity.


We dig into major issues and user needs, and how those needs can be addressed in current and future development. We also discuss hot topics from the Project Teams Gathering, and major development decisions agreed by the team.


Get an in-depth look at the top features and enhancements Cinder plans to deliver in the Pike release in August. Then look beyond Pike to the Queens and “R” releases to learn more about major development themes such as scalability, manageability, resiliency and user experience that the team intends to tackle in the long term.


Developers who are interested in contributing to this project are strongly encouraged to attend, as are users and product managers who want to know more about this project’s latest features, their value to users, and the development team’s roadmap.

Questions and discussion are encouraged from the audience, and this presentation will become part of OpenStack’s project navigator at openstack.org/software/project-navigator.

materials.title: Project Update - Cinder

events.title: Red Hat - Meet Your New Managed Private Cloud from Red Hat and IBM
events.body:
Red Hat and IBM recently partnered together to announce IBM Bluemix Private Cloud with Red Hat, a managed Red

Hat OpenStack Platform environment hosted in an IBM Cloud data center. This strategic collaboration is designed to

help enterprises benefit from the OpenStack platform’s speed and economics while more easily extending their

existing Red Hat virtualized and cloud workloads to the IBM Private Cloud offering. In this session, we will explore the

architecture of the offering as well as exploring additional open source enteprise solutions that can be deployed on top of the Bluemix Private Cloud infrastructure.

materials.title: Red Hat - Meet Your New Managed Private Cloud from Red Hat and IBM

events.title: Running a Scientific Application on an OpenStack Cloud
events.body:
The scientific community is still largely wedded to a traditional HPC compute model where a task scheduler provisions bare metal nodes and the application runs directly on the node OS. Typically, the application is restricted to using the node's software libraries and compiler toolchain. In our experience this compute model causes the development environment on the HPC cluster and the user's desktop to differ, adding obstacles to software development. In addition, cluster software upgrades potentially alter the application's runtime behavior or results.

From our point of view the provisioning of virtual machines in OpenStack offers a user friendly alternative. But how does a scientific application perform on OpenStack?

Here we run a quantum chemistry application employing novel computational algorithms written in Fortran and MPI and investigate the changes necessary in the work flow and the application code and the impact of virtualization on performance and parallel scalability.
events.learning: We looked at how much effort it is to run a scientific research code on an OpenStack cloud and what the performance and parallel scaling impact was.

materials.title: Running a Scientific Application on an OpenStack Cloud

events.title: Show Me My Packet Log: Neutron Packet Logging with Monasca
events.body:
This presentation introduces the network traffic logging feature which is

proposed to Neutron, and explain by demonstration how it works,

especially gathering log data using Monasca.

 

OpenStack network is highly virtualized by Neutron, and therefore it is

very difficult to understand how network packets are processed. A

traffic log is necessary to investigate network problem. We introduce a

packet logging feature to monitor the behaviors of Security Group at

network ports.  This feature is helpful to make sure network access rules

work as expected, and troubleshoot network problems easier.

 

To manage the logs in a centralized way we leverage Monasca's

Logging-as-a-Service functionality. Using it all the queries that are

performed are scoped to a tenant/project, so that every user can access

only his data.

 

In this presentation we will give a demonstration of this feature and show

how you can see network packet logs using Monasca.
events.learning:
Attendees can learn as follows:

  • An architecture and usage of Neutron packet logging feature
  • Operations that show how to manage logging data in cloud system by using Neutron and Monasca

materials.title: Show Me My Packet Log: Neutron Packet Logging with Monasca

events.title: The 5G Network: A Glimpse Into the Connected Future
events.body:
There’s a lot of buzz surrounding the potential for 5G to completely change the technology landscape and enable massive connectivity and IOT. But what is 5G really? What is the market opportunity for 5G and what infrastructure is needed to support it?

This panel, moderated by Phil Robb, Interim Executive Director of OpenDaylight, will bring together executives to discuss:

* The new enhancements in 5G and what they will enable 
* The infrastructure needed to support 5G, including SDN and NFV 
* The market opportunity for 5G including new applications like autonomous driving, smart cities and e-health practices like remote surgery 
* Who will profit from 5G, and what kinds of new business models will emerge
events.learning:
This panel, moderated by Neela Jacques, Executive Director of OpenDaylight, will bring together executives from AT&T, Ericsson, Verizon and Huawei to discuss:

  • The new enhancements in 5G and what they will enable
  • The infrastructure needed to support 5G, including SDN and NFV
  • The market opportunity for 5G including new applications like autonomous driving, smart cities and e-health practices like remote surgery
  • Who will profit from 5G, and what kinds of new business models will emerge

materials.title: The 5G Network: A Glimpse Into the Connected Future

events.title: Who Left the Lights on Again?  Dealing with Inefficient Cloud Usage
events.body: So your organization has adopted the cloud.  You've been tasked with deployment of an hybrid model.  Great! You have your OpenStack cloud and your public cloud... then you find out your organization is relying on a second Cloud Service Provider, then a third.  The all of the sudden, the CFO drops in your office asking what's up with all of the rising costs?  Who is monitoring those virtual systems being idle?  How do you get development team to adopt a responsible use of resources that are eating away at your operational budget? These are all questions that we had to address in our journey to the cloud.  Come learn some of the simple and not-so-simple solutions we have deployed to optimize our usage.
events.learning: How an internal cloud brokerage approach can help manage costs and ensure that optimal usage is made of both the OpenStack cloud and the various public providers using techniques to monitor usage, increase workload density and tracking costs.

materials.title: Who Left the Lights on Again?  Dealing with Inefficient Cloud Usage

events.title: Your Cloud is Amazing, so Why Aren’t You Running Everything on It?
events.body: Bloomberg announced our Openstack-based cloud about 4 years ago, but creating our dream infrastructure was quicker than refactoring thousands of applications to run on it. A significant mindset shift is necessary to escape the confines of typical big-company enterprise IT infrastructure for a future that’s developer and agility-focused. We’ll talk about three important ways you can support the needed change.

materials.title: Your Cloud is Amazing, so Why Aren’t You Running Everything on It?

events.title: Docs/I18n - Project Onboarding
events.body: The project onboarding rooms will be set up classroom style, dedicated to the projects that have signed up to teach new contributors about the project code, and give them an opportunity to meet established community members. The idea is that new contributors will come here to get started in the project after they have gone to OpenStack Upstream Institute and already know the basics of contribution. *Come here to involve contribution with Alexandra Settle - Docs team PTL and Ian Y. Choi - I18n team PTL!*

events.title: Hands-On Lab: Octavia
events.body:
In this interactive workshop, memebers of the Octavia team will walk attendees through the installation and configuration of Octavia, the Open Stack LoadBalancer, on a prepared virtual machine in the cloud. Attendees will leave with an understanding of the various components of Octavia, how to configure and tune the controller and the amphora, and with some troubleshooting tips.

Attendees will learn: 

  • Octavia Architecture 101
  • How to Install and Configure Octavia
  • How to perform day to day Octavia operations tasks
  • End user usage of the API, CLI and Horizon UI
  • Tips and Tricks for using Octavia
  • Contributing to Octavia 101

Please note:  session attendance does have a maximum capacity.  All admittance will be on a first come, first served basis.  Thank you for your understanding.
events.learning:
• Octavia Architecture 101
  • How to Install and Configure Octavia
  • How to perform day to day Octavia operations tasks
  • End user usage of the API, CLI and Horizon UI
  • Tips and Tricks for using Octavia
  • Contributing to Octavia 101

events.title: Hierachical Quotas
events.body: It looks like we might finally be getting traction on Hierarchical Quotas. Use this as a validation point for the Limits approach and the Quota models we've thus identified.\

events.title: OpenStack Kolla Ansible Hands-On Lab Session
events.body:
This hands-on lab session will provide an overview of OpenStack Kolla and deployment using Ansible and Docker Containers.  Each participant will get a virtualbox image (Kolla All-In-One).  Docker images created via Kolla-Build will be included.  The OpenStack environment is CentOS based with OVS bridge and LVM Cinder.


The hands-on lab will cover the following:

1) Take a look at the list of OpenStack docker containers
2) Create heat stack
     - Check that cinder volume can be attached to VM
     - Check that we are able to SSH and ping the VM
     - Look at log files in Heka container that are useful for troubleshooting

3) Destroy current environment and rebuild environment with Kolla Ansible playbooks

4) Go through basic configurations in globals.yml

5) Execute Kolla Health Check scripts to confirm successful redeployment

6) Kolla-Ansible multi-nodes deployment on KVM host
     - Multi-node configurations and local registry
     - Demo multimode deployment on KVM host
     - Create test VM

 

Please note:  session attendance does have a maximum capacity.  All admittance will be on a first come, first served basis.  Thank you for your understanding.
events.learning: The attendee will gain an overview of OpenStack Kolla, Ansible and Docker Containers.  The lab session will allow participants to have hands-on experience on Kolla Ansible and Docker.

events.title: Zun- Project Onboarding
events.body: The project onboarding rooms will be set up classroom style, dedicated to the projects that have signed up to teach new contributors about the project code, and give them an opportunity to meet established community members. The idea is that new contributors will come here to get started in the project after they have gone to OpenStack Upstream Institute and already know the basics of contribution.

events.title: Congratulations ${IT_GUY} you are now our Openstack Administrator.
events.body: Face it,  you are an awesome IT Administrator/Engineer.  From the menial to inherently complex you turn no reasonable task or project down.  You are suddenly approached by your manager telling you that you are now taking over the responsibilities as the company's Openstack Administrator/Engineer and he/she trusts you that you possess aptitude to quickly become a capable Openstack Administrator.   Your palms are sweaty, knees weak and  arms are heavy but they shouldn't be for too long as getting acquainted with an OpenStack cloud is not a complicated task as long as you are armed with the right tools. This visually rich presentation will cover the discovery and assessment of an Openstack cloud through the installation and use of the Openstack CLI utilities in order to help us newly minted Openstack Administrators familiarize ourselves with our newly inherited OpenStack powered clouds.
events.learning: Attendees are expected to learn as to how to properly discover, assess, and and learn their OpenStack infrastructure footprint through the use of the various OpenStack CLI utilities even with limited Openstack knowledge.

materials.title: Congratulations ${IT_GUY} you are now our Openstack Administrator.

events.title: Zconverter - 6 Must-Have Features for Hybrid or Multi-Cloud Migration or Cloud Recovery as a Service Among Heterogenous Cloud Platforms and/or Hypervisors
events.body:
This topic will talk about 6 must-have converting technology for hybrid cloud migration from public cloud to private openstack cloud or cloud-to-cloud migration among heterogeneous cloud platforms and/or hypervisors and/or disk formats and so on.

This is the subject which is also applied to OpenStack based Cloud Recovery as a Service.

materials.title: Zconverter - 6 Must-Have Features for Hybrid or Multi-Cloud Migration or Cloud Recovery as a Service Among Heterogenous Cloud Platforms and/or Hypervisors

events.title: Automation of End-to-End and Full Stack Testing of an OpenStack Cloud
events.body:
In a large multi-site OpenStack Cloud environment, we have been testing the building blocks in all layers for two year now.  We test these blocks individually as well as test end-to-end flows across them.

The building blocks that need to be tested include hardware, OS/VMMs, OpenStack, Contrail, other software, and IT tools.  These blocks are tested using their APIs, CLIs or GUIs.

We have automated a significant part of our testing using open source tools.  We leverage Tempest for testing OpenStack.  API tests for non-OpenStack components and extensions to Tempest (e.g., testing scenarios) are automated using OpenStack plugins.  We have been automating CLI tests using TestInfra and we have also been considering Puppet Facter.  We have automated testing of OpenStack Horizon and other GUIs using Selenium.

In addition describing our automation, we will share information on the number of tests we perform, our extent of automation and the benefits we have seen as well as some challenges.
events.learning:
The attendees will learn the following:

  • The requirements for testing all components of a large, multi-site OpenStack managed Cloud that has been in production for 2+ years.
  • The need for automated testing.
  • Automation of API testing using Tempest plugins with detailed examples.
  • Options for automating CLI testing with an in-depth look at TestInfra.
  • Automation of GUI testing using Selenium with examples.
  • The features supported by our Cloud and the numbers of test cases to be executed to effectively test our Cloud.
  • Where we are in our automation journey, the benefits we have seen so far and the challenges we have faced.

materials.title: Automation of End-to-End and Full Stack Testing of an OpenStack Cloud

events.title: Scalr - How To Self-Service Safely, Responsibly, and at Scale
events.body: Cloud Self-Service must be based on the understanding that enterprises have a wide spectrum of users, some users value ease of use, while some value operational freedom. In either case provisioning must be done a safe, responsible, and cost-effective way. In this session we'll talk about how enterprises deliver repeatable self-service workflows at scale, and match each user with the method that makes them most productive, all within the guardrails of company policy.

materials.title: Scalr - How To Self-Service Safely, Responsibly, and at Scale

events.title: Finding Needles in the Open Hay Stack
events.body: Customers rely on wireless and broadband more – and in more ways – than ever before. Verizon’s superior networks provide an edge in delivering the digital experiences that are vital to customers’ lives and businesses’ success. We’re also building the businesses of the future such as Internet of Things and digital commerce, based on Virtual Network Function (VNF) applications on OpenStack. Over the past 18 months logs have helped troubleshoot each layer: hardware, OpenStack, and VNF. OpenStack log use cases range from monitoring virtual infrastructure health to correlating details about a network element going down and network elements affected by the outage. Future use cases include security audits and providing confirmation of network activities.
events.learning: Telecommunications operators will learn of OpenStack log service assurance use cases from Verizon Wireless production and lab deployments. Use cases resolve issues at an individual layer with operational insight into how issues at one layer, for example OpenStack, affect another layer, for example, VNFs. Operators and architects will learn strategies for managing daily high log volumes in production. Strategies include optimizing search with advanced indexing and tagging, managing high log volumes with distributed processing, and compression. Operators will also learn how presenting logs in dynamic reporting dashboards can help solve specific functional use cases. Developers will learn ways to further improve OpenStack log value in production, such as continuing to refine log severity levels based on operational needs, and/or providing the capability for operators to do so. Telecommunications CEOs will learn how OpenStack logs support delivering a reliable OpenStack-based solution in production.

materials.title: Finding Needles in the Open Hay Stack

events.title: 7 "Must-Haves" for Highly Effective Telco NFV Deployments
events.body:
Red Hat and Juniper Networks will address 7 of the biggest challenges faced by Broadband NFV deployments

  1. Predictable high performance -  linearly scalable performance, low latency, hardware agnostic with acceleration, small  to jumbo frames
  2. High availability - No single point of failure, link bonding, redundancy, load balancing, failure detection, monitoring, live migration
  3. Superior L2 & L3 connectivity - Solid L2 networking, transition to L3 routing, external IPs, IPv6, carrier grade NAT
  4. Managed multi-tenancy - Isolation of north-south & east-west tenant networks; Manageable, scalable overlay tunnels
  5. Agile programmable infrastructure - Flexible datapath, integration with SDN controller, elastic network, auto-scaling
  6. Multi-site deployments - Geo-site deployments for better scale, redundancy and disaster recovery
  7. Distributed security - move security from edge to the application, distributed firewalls, connection tracking, L2 MACsec & L3 IPsec encrypted tunnels between endpoints
events.learning:
This presentation takes a deep dive into challenges faced by NFV Telco customers when moving to Openstack deployed virtualized solutions. Providing agile and scalable deployments with Openstack enables Telcos/ISPs to optimize usage of resources, deploy new services quickly and compete with higher value offerings

What will be covered?

  • Learn strategies and state of the art for deploying high performance VNFs with Openstack today
  • Red Hat and Juniper will address 7 of the biggest challenges faced by NFV deployments and why they are important to Telcos/ISPs
  • The presentation will have real world Telco/ISP deployment scenarios for the Broadband and SD-WAN usecase.  
  • It will cover issues  encountered along with workarounds and solutions provided which maybe still work in progress.
  • It will cover futuristic roadmap and requirements for Broadband NFV deployments for the next 2-3 years.

materials.title: 7 "Must-Haves" for Highly Effective Telco NFV Deployments

events.title: Across the Hybrid Cloud with Karbor
events.body:
While "cloud-native" is gaining ground, most enterprise applications are still not there. But there’s no reason why such applications should miss out on the benefits of hybrid cloud.

Karbor Application Data Protection can be used to migrate an application from on-prem OpenStack to off-prem and vice versa.

Extensible architecture enables users to plug-in new backends and new resource types into Karbor and leverage all vendor-specific capabilities without compromising the ability to protect the data and ensure service continuity.

In this session we will introduce Karbor and showcase how it could be used in a cloud migration scenario.
events.learning: Attendees should expect to be familiar with a new way of moving their application around the clouds with Karbor, an OpenStack big-tent project.

materials.title: Across the Hybrid Cloud with Karbor

events.title: Advanced Controller Optimization: How to Get the Most of Your Controllers
events.body:
OpenStack controllers are essential components of every single installation, this ia a well known axiom. But depending on type of installation, controllers can host entire OpenStack installation or only some of the services which characteristics vary widely. On my session I am going to show you:

  1. OpenStack controller workload characteristics, there is no one which fits all.
  2. How to detect basic hardware configuration issues and how to optimize our existing hardware?
  3. What is really running on my CPUs and how can I make it faster?
  4. IRQ who does generate them? and who does serve them? can we make it faster?
  5. OpenStack processes CPU affinity.
  6. Understanding of disk controllers IO and optimization ways.
  7. Network traffic, how does controller do it? From the packet on the wire to read()/write() calls in Python code.

This session is going to be a little bit more advanced than traditional how to on uptime, top, htop, iotop. It will explain how the things work under the hood.
events.learning:
• How to understand and estimate OpenStack controller workload type.
  • How to detect basic hardware configuration issues and how to optimize our existing hardware?
  • What is really running on my CPUs and how can I make it faster?
  • OpenStack processes CPU affinity, how to get the most of it?
  • Understanding of disk controllers IO and optimization ways (blktrace).
  • Network traffic, how does controller do it? From the packet on the wire to read()/write() calls in Python code.
  • IRQ who does generate them? and who does serve them? can we make it faster?

materials.title: Advanced Controller Optimization: How to Get the Most of Your Controllers

events.title: Ansible + OpenStack 101
events.body:
So you have spent months convincing your leadership to go with OpenStack.  Finally the keys of the cloud are turned over to you as the Cloud Operator, you then look over at your co-workers and say “now what”.  The next set of phrases normal are something like: Now how do we best administer this cloud?  Cloud is suppose to be easier, right?

 

Well: don’t worry, cloud can be easier and better depending on how you approach it.  As OpenStack has begun to be considered more of a mainstream cloud platform, the challenge of operating it after it is built has become prevalent.  While all cloud tasks can be executed via the API or CLI tool on a one by one basis, this would not be the best way to handle larger cloud deployments.  The need for more of an automated approach to administering OpenStack is now clear.  With the many IaaS capabilities OpenStack has to offer, the addition of Ansible - an easy to use configuration management tool -  you are assured of a more complete cloud implementation.

 

During this session we will review a few real-life OpenStack cloud operator examples and demonstrate how using Ansible to automate those tasks will drastically reduce the effort needed to maintain your cloud.

 

Audience Takeaways:

Discover some common day-to-day operator tasks

Learn why OpenStack and Ansible work great together

Review some automation considerations before getting started

Step thru how to automate a few of the operator tasks with Ansible

Benefits of adopting an ‘Administration DevOps’ state of mind and next steps

materials.title: Ansible + OpenStack 101

events.title: Canonical - Containerised OpenStack and Kubernetes: Running in 60 Minutes
events.body: A containerised control plane offer multiple advantages. Join this session to learn about the different ways of containerising the control plane, the pros and cons of each and how you can build OpenStack for testing on a single machine using containers. The session will feature a live demo of building OpenStack from scratch and deploying container based workloads in it. Should be a fun 45 mins!

materials.title: Canonical - Containerised OpenStack and Kubernetes: Running in 60 Minutes

events.title: Continuous Delivery with Spinnaker and OpenStack
events.body: Spinnaker is a Netflix open source project for building robust continuous delivery pipelines and managing a multi-cloud infrastructure footprint. The "cloud driver" in Spinnaker is capable of managing footprints across AWS, Google Cloud, Pivotal CloudFoundry, Azure, Oracle Cloud, and Openstack. This talk will discuss the reasons behind Spinnaker and showcase its ability to deliver software continuously in an Openstack private cloud.

materials.title: Continuous Delivery with Spinnaker and OpenStack

events.title: Evolving the User Survey
events.body: What elements of the User Survey are most helpful to your development team and/or business? What would you like to dig deeper into, and what would you like to change? This is an open forum to hear how we can continue to evolve the tenth semiannual User Survey for the benefit of the community.

events.title: Federation with Keycloak and FreeIPA
events.body:
Did you know you can use the open source Keycloak authentication portal to federate FreeIPA users through to the OpenStack dashboard? There are many benefits to this approach. FreeIPA user management provides a rich set of identity features across an enterprise (beyond just OpenStack), while also allowing a dashboard login option that does not reveal credentials to any OpenStack services.


In this session, we’ll provide an overview of the components involved in federation: OpenStack dashboard, Keystone, FreeIPA, and Keycloak. We’ll discuss how they work together, how they compare with direct LDAP authentication, and how to manually configure these components for federation. We’ll also provide a detailed overview of certificate requirements, a demonstration of federation in an OpenStack lab, and useful troubleshooting tips. In addition, we’ll describe opportunities for collaboration between teams, as a successful federation deployment may require buy-in from multiple stakeholders.
events.learning:
This talk begins with an overview of the components involved in the Federated Identity solution: Dashboard, Keystone, FreeIPA, and Keycloak

The Federated Identity overview then describes how these components work together. Then, a comparison with direct LDAP integration allows users to understand the differences with this approach.

A detailed overview of certificate requirements will help users understand the certificate requirements of federation, including how to get these components to agree on trusted certificates.

This is followed by descriptions of how to configure the individual components, with interesting points highlighted. Next is a demonstration of federation in an OpenStack lab, followed by some troubleshooting tips.

materials.title: Federation with Keycloak and FreeIPA

events.title: Future of configuration management in deployment tools
events.body:
Abstract: I would like to bring Developers and Operators in a room to discuss about future of Configuration Management in OpenStack.

Until now, we haven't done a good job in collaborating on how we make configuration management in a consistent way across OpenStack Deployment Tools.
Some efforts started to emerge in Pike: https://etherpad.openstack.org/p/deployment-pike
And some projects like TripleO started some discussion on future of configuration management: https://etherpad.openstack.org/p/tripleo-etcd-transition

In this discussion, we will discuss about our common challenges and take some actions from there, where projects could collaborate.

Desired people:
- Folks from Deployment Tools (TripleO, Kolla, OSA, Kubernetes, etc)
- Operators who deploy OpenStack

Moderator: Emilien Macchi

events.title: Hybrid Orchestration - Kubernetes on Bare Metal and OpenStack Demo
events.body:
There has been an explosion of application platforms in recent years, from containers, to virtualization, to cloud platforms. Often, each platform has its own orchestration tools to deal with automation requirements to serve the needs of DevOps teams. Real world environments usually consist of combinations of such platforms.

 

This session and demo will present orchestration that spans multiple platforms, in this case Kubernetes on bare metal and Openstack virtual machines.

events.title: Integration of Enterprise Monitoring Product, Senlin, and Mistral for Auto-Healing
events.body: This proposal is to share an industry practice of auto-healing with reliable failure detection, real time notification, flexible recovery action. Where, a reputed enterprise monitoring product is integrated as an example of how to leverage existing tools/products outside OpenStack and industry intelligence for failure detection; Senlin is used to receive notifications from the integrated monitor and to trigger the recover action; Mistral is integrated with Senlin to allow a complementary recovery comprised of users’ custom workflows, for good handling of error cases, task parallelism and branching, and Senlin’s built-in actions which can be customized by a user defined health policy. We will demonstrate how to take all the advantages of these components in the Auto-healing solution.
events.learning:
In this presentation, we will give an introduction and demonstration about how to integrate the enterprise product with OpenStack projects in order to take all the advantages of these components and achieve an industry practice of auto-healing. In more details, attendees will see:

(1) How to create and operate the alerts/notifications of the external enterprise monitor in OpenStack.

(2) How to trigger OpenStack recovery Action once notified by the external monitor.

(3) How to execute Mistral workflows for the recover purpose.

(4) How to use Senlin Policy for customization of the auto-healing loop.

materials.title: Integration of Enterprise Monitoring Product, Senlin, and Mistral for Auto-Healing

events.title: Panel: Enterprise Adoption of Kubernetes and Containers
events.body: Enterprises are increasingly wanting to consume OpenStack as a Managed Service to avoid the complexity of running it themselves.  As they adopt kubernetes, many view kubernetes on bare metal as an alternative to OpenStack for microservice workloads. We will explore kubernetes on bare metal and kubernetes on OpenStack for private clouds, what drives enterprise preference and perception, and the journey for these customers as their workloads and needs change over time.
events.learning:
Gain insight from industry luminaries on the questions for this panel. Understand where the experts agree, and perhaps where they don't.

Sample Questions for the Panel

  1. In a private data center context, initially enterprises are wanting to try kubernetes on bare metal without OpenStack.  True or False?  
  2. What interest do your see in Kubernetes, and what is driving customer behavior? 
  3. The Kubernetes community plug-in ecosystem is enabling multiple options for networking, storage and compute.  When is an IaaS layer like OpenStack something that should be introduced into a kubernetes microservice solution?  
  4. What workloads or factors come in to play when thinking about whether to run Kubernetes with or without an IaaS layer like OpenStack? 
  5. IaaS’ are all starting to look similar (AWS, OpenStack, GKE)… Does this mean Kubernetes on bare metal is just for market entry/experimentation, or do you see it as a viable alternative to Private Cloud on IaaS (OpenStack, VMWare, etc.)?
  6. From a Managed Services perspective, what does it look like to have separate solutions for Kubernetes on bare metal vs. Kubernetes on OpenStack?   
  7. Or are Managed Service providers focusing on including an underlying IaaS platform?  If so, why?

materials.title: Panel: Enterprise Adoption of Kubernetes and Containers

events.title: Project Update - Designate
events.body:
Join the Project Team Leader of Designate and core contributors for a “project update” reflecting current developments in the Pike cycle and discussion of future development activity.


We dig into major issues and user needs, and how those needs can be addressed in current and future development. We also discuss hot topics from the Project Teams Gathering, and major development decisions agreed by the team.


Get an in-depth look at the top features and enhancements Designate plans to deliver in the Pike release in August. Then look beyond Pike to the Queens and “R” releases to learn more about major development themes such as scalability, manageability, resiliency and user experience that the team intends to tackle in the long term.


Developers who are interested in contributing to this project are strongly encouraged to attend, as are users and product managers who want to know more about this project’s latest features, their value to users, and the development team’s roadmap.

Questions and discussion are encouraged from the audience, and this presentation will become part of OpenStack’s project navigator at openstack.org/software/project-navigator.

materials.title: Project Update - Designate

events.title: Red Hat - Cloud in the Era of Hybrid-Washing: What's Real & What's Not?
events.body: For the past few years cloud washing was a practice IT vendors used to paint their not-necessarily-cloudy products as cloud. It would be nice to say that the trend dissipated, but that is not the case. It has just morphed into hybrid cloud washing. Hybrid is everywhere. As companies weigh decisions about what workloads to move to the cloud, vendors are using the descriptor to persuade potential customers that their workloads will move “seamlessly” or “effortlessly” between their private cloud and some public cloud. If only saying it made it so. In this session, you will learn what is and what isn’t hybrid cloud, and why that matters to your cloud strategy. Also, we will discuss how to partner with Red Hat and other vendors to ensure your public, private or hybrid cloud architecture doesn’t forget about user experience, security and integration.

materials.title: Red Hat - Cloud in the Era of Hybrid-Washing: What's Real & What's Not?

events.title: Running Containerized Cloud Foundry on Magnum
events.body: In this talk we will demonstrate running a containerized Cloud Foundry system on top of OpenStack Magnum (using Kubernetes). We will talk about our experience containerizing Cloud Foundry and how it was made to work on Magnum, as well as running on other Kubernetes systems. We will be sharing interesting improvements and present the challenges of keeping highly available systems online and up-to-date.

materials.title: Running Containerized Cloud Foundry on Magnum

events.title: Swimming upstream – Doctor project case study
events.body: Based on the lifecycle of the OPNFV Doctor project, this case study shows how operator requirements “on paper” have successfully been realized step-by-step and in close cooperation with upstream community projects into a mature fault management framework. A demo of the solution had been presented in a keynote at the last OpenStack Summit. The talk will describe how we have worked in the OPNFV Doctor project and will provide some lessons learned on this journey. With significant experience now of working OPNFV requirements upstream to OpenStack, we’ll share best practices for submitting contributions upstream, how to best communicate, and how to overcome the primary challenges.

events.title: Verizon Product Case Study - OpenStack at the Edge
events.body:
Think OpenStack only works in data centers and test beds?   Think again.  Coming from the need to deliver an identical network service application experience in radically different environments, the Virtual Network Services (VNS) product uses OpenStack components as its underlying platform to create a massively distributed Network as a Service solution.  VNS is a portfolio of network services delivered in a flexible framework on x86 hardware allowing customers to choose the services, network architecture and delivery models that best suit their needs.

OpenStack can be used for products that are distributed out to remote sites, but massively distributed OpenStack architectures have been a difficult problem that cannot be solved without taking a radically different approach to delivering orchestration and integration tools.  The product team created an OpenStack environment that fit in small footprint yet still works with orchestration tools located in a global cloud.
events.learning:
During this session you will learn how OpenStack was adapted to solve thorny product issues such as:

  • The need to perform in a massively distributed (think thousands of global locations) environment.
  • The need to deliver network services to customers located both at remote locations and globally distributed Verizon owned data centers.
  • Complex vendor integration, product orchestration and service delivery requirements
  • Tight hardware limitations and cost constraints.
  • Integration of orchestration tools to automate service delivery

materials.title: Verizon Product Case Study - OpenStack at the Edge

events.title: When One Cloud is Not Enough: An Overview of Sites, Regions, Edges, Distributed Clouds, and More
events.body:
As OpenStack becomes ubiquitous, organizations have reason to deploy multiple OpenStack clouds, sites, regions, "edges," or to distribute computing, to list a few possibilities and terms. These requirements could be based on capacity, latency, geographic location, high availability, other needs, or a combination of any or all.

But how should these varied and complex OpenStack systems be designed, deployed, and managed? What should the architecture be? Or even more basic, what to these terms mean, and who uses what definition and how do they differ? As we will show, even the nomenclature is difficult, as there are several major architectures, use-cases, and groups to be considered.

We will present an overview of the various options, projects, and decision points for this topic and detail the positives and negatives of various approaches, as well as what the gaps are in terms of solutions
events.learning: Attendees to this presentation should come away with a good understanding of common terminology, uses-cases, and architectures concerning organizational requirements which depend on deploying multiple OpenStack Clouds, regions, sites, edges, distributed compute, or other similar architectures. We hope attendees will be able to go back to their organizations and recognize requirements that suggest the aforementioned architectures may be needed, what the benefits and issues are, and in doing so are able to help the organization make informed decisions.

materials.title: When One Cloud is Not Enough: An Overview of Sites, Regions, Edges, Distributed Clouds, and More

events.title: Finding Needles in the Open Hay Stack
events.body: SevOne, a leader in network and infrastructure management, has partnered with a major US service provider, a leader in deploying production virtual network functions, to deliver service assurance for OpenStack-based infrastructure. Over the past 18 months, the SevOne solution has delivered expanding actionable insight into each ETSI layer: VNF, NFVI and MANO. This discussion will focus on OpenStack VIM service assurance and how the SevOne solution has been applied to real-world requirements; resource monitoring, service response, endpoint availability, workload utilization and closed loop automation. The discussion will conclude with an operational summary of the solution’s response to a compute blade down event. This example demonstrates how SevOne provides insights to various OpenStack outage symptoms, such as Nova compute metrics, Ceilometer performance metrics and OpenStack logs, to deduce root cause, service impact and even automate corrective action.
events.learning: Telecommunications operators will learn of OpenStack service assurance use cases from real world production deployments. Use cases resolve issues at an individual layer with operational insight into how issues at one layer, for example how OpenStack, affects another layer, for example, VNFs. Operators and architects will learn strategies to expose actionable alerts in production. Strategies such as presenting alerts in dynamic reporting dashboards focused on specific functional use cases. Developers will learn ways to further improve OpenStack data ingestion in production using advanced stream data modeling techniques. Telecommunications CEOs will learn how OpenStack service assurance can deliver a reliable OpenStack-based solution in production.

materials.title: Finding Needles in the Open Hay Stack

events.title: Analyst Relations Working Group Debrief
events.body: The Analyst Relations Working Group collaborates on ways to improve relationships between the OpenStack community and industry analysts. The group is particularly involved in planning analyst activities for OpenStack Summits. Whether you are a veteran member of the group or just want to see what the ARWG is all about, join us in Boston as we debrief on Summit analyst events and plan our strategy for the next six months, leading up to the OpenStack Summit in Sydney.

events.title: Strategies for Migrating Workloads from VMware to OpenStack
events.body:
As OpenStack adoption increases, companies are looking at ways to migrate workloads from traditional virtualization solutions like VMware or System Center to cloud infrastructures based on OpenStack. 

There are multiple angles to this problem to consider:

  • Pets vs Cattle: when is OpenStack the right choice and when not
  • Lift and shift: when is worth to use automated migration tools like Coriolis to move virtual machines
  • App migration: when to migrate individual applications and their data to a new platform (e.g. a PaaS)
  • Re-develop: when to adopt modern paradigms like microservices, containers etc and redevelop applications

There's no one-size-fits-all answer, but knowing what your options are, you can do the right choice for each use case. Costs also have a big impact, for example it can be worth to lift-and-shift and use the saved money to re-architect the next app generation.

We will also do a fully automated lift-and-shift and DRaaS live demo using the Coriolis project.
events.learning:
Attendees will learn about the best and fastest routes to adopt an OpenStack cloud infrastructure for existing workloads and perform informed decisions on the strategy to adopt.

Attendees will also learn how to use automated tools to perform migrations effortlessly.

materials.title: Strategies for Migrating Workloads from VMware to OpenStack

events.title: ARM - OpenStack and Containers on ARM: Status and Plans
events.body: In this brief, fast paced and informative session you'll receive an update on recent ARM powered server hardware and software ecosystem progress. One of the world's largest cloud providers recently disclosed their plans to deploy ARM based servers expressing that >50% of their data center could be powered by ARM! Last year Linaro took to the main stage in Barcelona representing the ARM partnership alongside 15 other companies as part of the OpenStack Interop challenge. Building on that foundation Linaro are now active members of the Kolla project to containerize OpenStack and have been busy working on DPDK in containerized environments too! In this session we'll hear from them about the journey, status and what's next! If you miss this session please don't hesitate to stop by our booth where we'll be more than willing to address your questions and tell you more about what we're up to.

materials.title: ARM - OpenStack and Containers on ARM: Status and Plans

events.title: 10 SDN solutions for OpenStack in 10 minutes
events.body:
First the presentation will kick off with a quick explanation on WHY the need of an SDN solution in OpenStack

The objective is to compare 10 different approches to SDN in Openstack. Each approach would be focusen in the way one SDN vendor proposes to integrate their product with Openstack.

This presentation is vendor neutral, it does not focus on pitching one particular vendor over another.

1 of the approches will be of course Neutron stand-alone as an SDN.
events.learning: Learn to differentiate and compare when selecting and SDN solution for their Openstack cloud deployments. The idea is to give the attendees an idea of the questions they should be asking their SDN vendor.

materials.title: 10 SDN solutions for OpenStack in 10 minutes

events.title: Gigamon Visibility Platform for NFVI Architecture and Multi-Tenant Private Clouds
events.body:
As Tier-1 Service Providers transform and optimize their core mobile networks from using physical functions to VNF (Virtual Network Functions) or large enterprises adopt multi-tenant private clouds for IaaS deployments, visibility and monitoring is paramount in being able to demonstrate interoperability, compliancy and security.

However, traditional monitoring tools that provide the KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) for voice analysis or security for east-west blind spots, have had no way to access the traffic in an open and agnostic fashion, without breaking tenant boundaries.

In this session, we will cover how Gigamon in using the OpenStack community project Tap-as-a-Service (TaaS), allows customers to
Analyze and troubleshoot subscriber traffic, especially for the mobile operator
Provide network visibility for IDS, forensics, SIEM etc.
Ensure SLAs and compliancy for the applications that have migrated
Leverage existing traffic and packet-based monitoring and tooling infrastructure (CAPEX/OPEX savings)
De-risk the impact of rolling out new & largely untried NFVI technologies

materials.title: Gigamon Visibility Platform for NFVI Architecture and Multi-Tenant Private Clouds

events.title: Building and Operating a Swift S3 Storage Environment as a Service Provider
events.body:
In the service provider world, data is infinite and constant. It is constantly growing, constantly evolving, and companies are constantly changing the way they want to interact with it. To sustain and manage the customer demand Expedient had to get creative in how they store customer data. Running PB of block storage to run VM's and Containers was easy but customers are demanding programmable storage via a S3 API. Which presents a whole new set of challenges especially when you have to interact with both modes of IT, traditional and cloud.

To meet customers needs, Expedient leveraged OpenStack Swift(SwiftStack version) to provide that API driven storage. See the blue prints we used to build our offering, learn about how our customers are adopting it, and hear our experiences after operating this platform for two years. Many of our early assumptions were wrong and caused us some pain that you can quickly avoid.
events.learning: After this session, you will have an understanding on what an object storage platform could do for you, examples of how you can use it, and a path to get you started regardless of what software package you use.

materials.title: Building and Operating a Swift S3 Storage Environment as a Service Provider

events.title: Cloud Native Computing with Kubernetes and OpenStack
events.body: Kubernetes is an 'Open Source hit', with over 1,000 contributors and based on the experience of developers running one of the world's largest computing platform inside Google. In this talk, David Aronchick, senior product manager for Google Container Engine and Kubernetes, will discuss the history of the technology, the decision to open source the software and how it will be part of a computing revolution combining hybrid cloud, virtualized applications and cloud-native distributed systems. David will discuss how OpenStack and Kubernetes are better together and the future roadmap.

materials.title: Cloud Native Computing with Kubernetes and OpenStack

events.title: Containerizing OpenStack Deployments: Lessons Learned from TripleO
events.body:
There are multiple tools that allow for deploying OpenStack on containers. Some of these tools started from scratch with contianers in mind, some others broke backwards compatibility and some others are aiming for a smooth transition from host based deployment to a containerized one.

TripleO is undergoing the transition from a baremetal to a containerized deployment and it's already overcome several challenges related to this process. This presentation aims to share the technical challenges from a deployment and operations perspective that are common to every containers based OpenStack deployment. The experiences that will be shared go from config management to volumes and network administration.
events.learning:
• How to migrate from non-containerized deployment to a containerized deployment
  • How to manage storage for containers
  • How to manage dynamic config generation for OpenStack deployments
  • How to distribute and group containers in a containers based OpenStack deployment

materials.title: Containerizing OpenStack Deployments: Lessons Learned from TripleO

events.title: Demonstrate the Efficient Strategy to Backup OpenStack Resources
events.body:
Backup the OpenStack is always a big and open challenge for operator or admin. If we do not have good solution then it is very painful and time consuming. One of the key goal of operators is to keep taking Cloud backup and make sure about user data and usability.

Very first and important question to achieve this goal is "Hey! What Backup Solution we can use?"

Based on some PoC and feasibility tests on different backup solution, we fetched some of the interesting results. This will definitely help audience to find out answer to their open question about backup solution. 

In this talk we will present our experience in backup area with all possible solution currently we have in market. Also we would like to talk about key features which must be included in those solution.
events.learning: Operator and admin can get the best strategy and solution to Backup the OpenStack resources which eventually will save their time and manual effort.

materials.title: Demonstrate the Efficient Strategy to Backup OpenStack Resources

events.title: Deploying Cloud Foundry Services to OpenStack with the Apache Brooklyn Service Broker
events.body:
The Open Service Broker API provides a means of adding new services to your Cloud Foundry application, but usually that means creating a new service broker for each additional service. In this talk, we demonstrate the Brooklyn service broker, which utilizes the open source application blueprinting and management platform Apache Brooklyn to deploy a multitude of services on OpenStack with a single service broker.

In this talk, Robert Moss will give examples of services from a range of NoSQL and analytics platforms in the Apache Brooklyn catalog. He will show how to use existing components in the Brooklyn ecosystem to create new Cloud Foundry services that are deployed to OpenStack and autonomically managed by Apache Brooklyn.

materials.title: Deploying Cloud Foundry Services to OpenStack with the Apache Brooklyn Service Broker

events.title: Deprecation of Postgresql
events.body: Context: https://review.openstack.org/#/c/427880/

events.title: Designing Cloud Native Applications - Deep dive
events.body:
The twelve factors

The twelve-factor app is a methodology for building apps that can fully utilize the cloud capabilities and much more. Some of this discipline is enforced on applications orchestrated using Cloud foundry or Kubernetes running on OpenStack.

Case study

We dive deep into the patterns of a highly scalable architecture with examples, showcasing how Cisco's Cloud IWAN was designed to be cloud native and its successful migration from Cloud Foundry to Kubernetes based deployment.

Microservice architecture

Architecting software, as microservices that are highly scalable and portable, has its own pros and cons. We want to share how we overcame the cons with the product under consideration.

Anti-patterns

Common failures & mistakes while designing large enterprise applications, limit the capabilities of the application to be truly cloud native. We share how not to design/refactor few components.

All these learnings are applicable for any product we want to be cloud native.
events.learning:
From beginners to advanced application developers and designers, the key takeaways are,

  • Microservice architecture - pros and cons. How to overcome the cons?
  • Steps to deploy applications on Cloud Foundry running on OpenStack.
  • Steps to deploy applications on Kubernetes running on OpenStack.
  • How to refactor an application to make it truly cloud native?
  • What are the anti-patters while designing such a large application?
  • Design a large and highly scalable enterprise application.
  • Insight into the ELK stack and how it is used in the application under consideration.
  • Insight into Cisco's Network Services Orchestrator.

materials.title: Designing Cloud Native Applications - Deep dive

events.title: Experience with DPDK Troubleshooting
events.body:
Getting near real-time performance for VNF applications requires designing the application carefully and profiling its performance under realistic conditions. OpenStack has developed many functionalities that helps in this, such as CPU and PCI topology awareness and pinning the virtual machines to dedicated cores. The host networking stack, in turn, has been optimized with features such as accelerated virtual switches and DPDK.

This presentation gives an update of using DPDK in real VNF tests and tells some real life experiences from DPDK troubleshooting.

materials.title: Experience with DPDK Troubleshooting

events.title: Making keystone consumable outside of OpenStack
events.body:
Keystone provides a multi-tenancy framework, which has become an important and common model throughout OpenStack. There are projects that would like to use that model in other non-OpenStack environments and software.

What changes can we make to allow more projects outside OpenStack to consume keystone?

events.title: MOC Simple GUI: An "And" to OpenStack Horizon
events.body:
The Massachusetts Open Cloud (MOC) needs a simple intuitive GUI for its public cloud marketplace. Our goal is to provide a tool to enhance the user experience by automating mundane but complicated steps to use cloud resources.

OpenStack Horizon is inadequate to serve naive users who lack basic cloud knowledge and to whom the cloud is simply a tool to get computing results for their scientific research. This new GUI serves to be a simpler tool streamlining the cloud experience. It can be used by itself or alongside Horizon. Developing a new GUI from scratch can be both time-consuming and challenging. A collaboration with the Cyverse’s Atmosphere/Troposphere project has helped accelerate the development of the MOC Simple GUI. 

An overview of the design of the MOC simple GUI will be presented. The divergence from the upstream Atmosphere/Troposphere design to enhance security, and allow interoperability with Horizon will be discussed.
events.learning:
• complication of graphical interface design/development of public cloud marketplace and 
  • components of MOC Simple GUI: already available Django apps; relevant Python library such as libcloud and Rtwo

materials.title: MOC Simple GUI: An "And" to OpenStack Horizon

events.title: NetApp - The Importance of Data Management for NFV: Use Cases That Need Persistent Storage
events.body:
Architects designing NFV deployments focus most of their time on providing robust network, compute and automation layers, while considering the challenges of operating at scale. 

What is often neglected during the planning process are the real world requirements for persistent storage to provide their services. As architects move from designing customized to designing standardized and automated stacks, it will become more important to provide a flexible, yet easy to maintain, storage architecture that can guarantee performance for each application in a NFV deployment.  

Looking forward, network functions are going to hosted in different formats: physical, virtualized, containerized, potentially even from the public cloud. How can we make sure all these flavors can coexist all together, without forcing us to re-architect our current storage setups?

materials.title: NetApp - The Importance of Data Management for NFV: Use Cases That Need Persistent Storage

events.title: neutron multi-site
events.body: What choices would one make to provide a neutron multi-site architecture, ie. one where N geographically dispersed data centers were used to build an openstack cloud?

events.title: Next Generation, Open Source vCPE Framework
events.body:
The vision of being able to consume, configure and manage the WAN Network, and services that come with it, through a set of self-service portals and automation tools, has made vCPE the most common use case in the NFV space. Another major driver behind this motion is the promise of cost savings. For the enterprise IT guys it is the savings that come from being able to use low cost CPE devices and network services that are delivered over the top. For CSPs it is about eliminating site visits, creating flexible service options, automating service creation, and virtualizing assets.

 

However, the reality is a lot more complex, and we encountered situations where the vCPE services failed to deliver on the promised savings and, in some cases, were even more expensive and of inferior quality.

 

This talk will demystify the vCPE cost model and offer an alternative way of building a vCPE solution that is not only more cost effective but also innovative and future proof while providing the flexibility and adaptability that CSPs need in order to remain relevant in this fast changing landscape.

events.title: NFV Management and Network Orchestartion (MANO) Using OpenStack
events.body:
There are several Open Source orchestration projects that integrate with OpenStack as the VIM. The OPNFV MANO working group has been working with several of them to develop common integration requirements, data models, and APIs. These include OpenStack upstream OPNFV , OPEN-O, OpenBaton and evaluate many more as the consistant approach emerges.

The Panel will provide insight on OpenStack requirements from their vantage points based on their workloads, VNF best practices and market perspective. The Panel will be moderated by Randy Levensalor.
events.learning: What is the precption of normative ETSI specifiction of MANO versus the reality in Open Source support in OpenStack and its upstreams in OPNFV, OPEN-O, OpenBaton, integration architecture. Why is that so many MANO stacks are required and what best pracices will help them interoperate based on Service VNFs that are composed from functional modules, legacy as well emerging ones. The panel members will provie their respective view porints and OPNFV community would like to learn and move the efforts to a acceptable common minimums to enable Interoperability and colloaboration through OpenStack community.

events.title: Securing Microservice Interactions in OpenStack and Kubernetes
events.body:
Interacting microservices have a large dynamic attack surface from exposed APIs, communication channels, data-store interactions, and agile deployment. Communication between Kubernetes pods and OpenStack VMs further expands the attack surface. An ideal security solution will go beyond reachability and allow rich security services to be activated on demand. This talk will cover:

  • Review OpenStack mechanisms to secure inter-service communication in tenant networks, across K8s and OpenStack clusters, at both network and application layers, e.g. Kuryr, service insertion, FWaaS, Barbican, Congress.
  • Inter-operation of K8s and OpenStack mechanisms, e.g. K8s network policy & Neutron security groups.
  • Operational challenges of configuring infrastructure security mechanisms to achieve service-level security objectives, and methodology to mitigate challenges.
  • Outline and demo of a security approach that operates independently of infrastructure mechanisms to secure inter-service communications.
events.learning:
• A review of current OpenStack mechanisms to secure inter-service communication in tenant networks across Kubernetes and OpenStack clusters. Relevant mechanisms are at both the network and application layers, e.g., Kuryr, service insertion, FWaaS, Barbican, Congress.
  • Inter-operation of Kubernetes and OpenStack mechanisms, e.g., Kubernetes network policy and Neutron security groups.
  • Operational challenges of configuring infrastructure security mechanisms to achieve service-level security objectives, and a methodology to mitigate these challenges.
  • Outline and demo of a security approach that operates independently of infrastructure-level mechanisms to secure inter-service communications.

materials.title: Securing Microservice Interactions in OpenStack and Kubernetes

events.title: The U.S. Army Cyber School OpenStack Use Case: Saving Millions and Making Changes for the Benefit of National Defense
events.body:
The United States Army Cyber School (USACYS) is charged with training and educating Soldiers to defend the interests of the United States and our allies at home and abroad via means grounded in computer science, electrical engineering, robotics, physics, and mathematics.  Over the past 18 months, USACYS has used OpenStack to execute this critical mission for force readiness.

This presentation will focus on our journey from 3 borrowed servers connected to users via CAT6 cables running through a drop ceiling to a 2000-core cluster backed by a 4PB Ceph array that is 100% code-driven.  We will also discuss our CI pipeline that integrates our Blackboard LMS, Heat, and our asciidoc-based curriculum-as-code repository into a student experience that is always up-to-date, relevant, and technically accurate while investing minimum man-hours for content curation.  This DevOps-oriented approach, underpinned by OpenStack, allows our instructors to focus on teaching students and creating new content, not creating slide presentations and formatting word processor documents.  This approach has yielded high benefits in courseware quality and student outcomes while saving millions of dollars in platform TCO expenses.  The OpenStack solution has put USACYS years ahead of similar government education programs and on track to continue to embrace innovation and change for the benefit of national defense.

events.title: Ansible Lightning Talks
events.body:
A terrific trio of lightning talks about Ansible and OpenStack, from Clint Byrum, Doug Hellman, and Lars Kellogg-Stedman.

 

  • Bonny CI: Ansiturtles All The Way Down (Clint Byrum)

    • Abstract:

With BonnyCI, we are working to provide Zuul as a service to the broader

open source world.

 

Zuul is a system that OpenStack's development infrastructure uses

to schedule and orchestrate test resources across repositories and

interact with them via Ansible.

 

To deploy Zuul and its support systems, we use Ansible in the most

germane way.

 

And to provision computers/disks/networks/etc. for all of that, we use

Ansible's os_* modules to provision resources on our OpenStack cloud.

 

And since we believe in testing deployments, we test our own deployment

with BonnyCI itself.

 

In summary: we're using Ansible to provision computers to run Ansible

on to deploy a CI system that runs Ansible to deploy and test Ansible

that deploys a CI system that runs Ansible to test software.

 

In this talk we'll discuss:

 

- How not to go cross eyed when you find that you have Ansi-turtles

- Do the os_* modules really work and how can we best use them?

- Best practices for deploying apps with Ansible into a cloud

 

  • Moving Workloads Between OpenStack Clouds with Ansible (Doug Hellmann)

    • Abstract:  This presentation will describe a new tool that can be used to move tenant workloads out of one OpenStack cloud and import them into another cloud, using ansible playbooks as the intermediate data format. The tool is being created as part of a suite of tools for managing migrations for upgrades, but can also be used to move between public cloud providers or to capture in a playbook the configuration steps performed manually through the OpenStack UI. The presentation will cover design constraints, use cases, and implementation details of the tool and the playbooks it generates.

  • Driving OpenStack with Ansible: Jenkins + Ansible + Heat (Oh my!) (Lars Kellogg-Stedman)

    • Abstract: An overview of how we use Ansible as part of a Jenkins workflow to build disk images, provision a test environment using Heat, and then run validation tests on the Nova instances we just created, including practical examples of how to use the Ansible OpenStack modules.

events.title: Cinder Stands Alone
events.body:
Cinder is a powerful Software Defined Storage (SDS) service that is an integral part of OpenStack.  The real power from Cinder comes from its abstraction API that allows many storage solutions to work from the same API.  Cinder's API works with both open source and commercial storage solutions, and Cinder has over 70 drivers to support a variety of back end storage . With Cinder as a Software Defined Storage solution a user can perform basic volume operations like create, attach, and snapshot, without knowing the details of the backend storage array.
Did you know you can use Cinder as a standalone service, without any other OpenStack services running?  In this presentation we will cover how to deploy Cinder without the other OpenStack services and how you can create volumes and use them. Consumers can use Stand Alone Cinder for performing basic volume operations on Virtual Machines, Containers with a workflow using Docker or Kubernetes, or Bare Metal machines.
events.learning:
Attendess will learn:

  • How to setup Cinder to stand alone, with no other OpenStack services running.
  • How to configure standalone Cinder SDS for various storage backends.
  • How to use Cinder to create, attach, and snapshot volumes.
